articles.title: Sara Duterte trial: Confi fund admission may violate anti-alias law
articles.summary: The anti-alias law as amended states that persons wanting to use an alias must obtain judicial authority, and must still affix their real name in documents

blocks.text: Photos from Jire Carreon/Rappler, House screenshot; Illustration by Raffy de Guzman/Rappler
The anti-alias law as amended states that persons wanting to use an alias must obtain judicial authority, and must still affix their real name in documents

items: Vice President Sara Duterte's camp claims that recipients of her office's confidential funds used aliases, raising questions about potential violations of the anti-alias law.
Prosecutors argue that the use of aliases in acknowledgment receipts may constitute a violation of the law, which carries penalties including jail time and fines.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
For the first time, the camp of Vice President Sara Duterte made the claim that the recipients of her offices’ confidential funds used aliases.

It’s a plausible explanation that could justify the oddity of the names of the signatories on the acknowledgment receipts — from surnames of senators to a mix of brand names, such as the infamous Mary Grace Piattos.
This, however, raises another question: did Sara Duterte, as head of agency for the Office of the Vice President and previously the Department of Education, violate the anti-alias law?
The prosecution believes so.
“This does not fall under any of the exemptions to the Anti-Alias Law. This could be yet another case or violation against them,” public prosecutor Joel Chua said.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte trial: Confi fund admission may violate anti-alias law

blocks.text: What does the law actually say? The original law dates back to 1936, when the National Assembly of the Philippines passed Commonwealth Act No. 142. It was extensively amended by Republic Act 6085 in 1969.
The amended law prohibits a person from using any name other than the one he was registered with at birth, or the one he was baptized with, or the substitute name approved by a competent court.
The only exceptions are pseudonyms “solely for literary, cinema, television, radio or other entertainment purposes and in athletic events.”
If persons wants to use an alias, they need to obtain judicial authority to do so. They also cannot have more than one alias.

“The judicial authority for the use of alias the Christian name and the alien immigrant’s name shall be recorded in the proper local civil registry, and no person shall use any name or names other, than his original or real name unless the same is or are duly recorded in the proper local civil registry,” the law reads.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte trial: Confi fund admission may violate anti-alias law

blocks.text: RA 6085 also explicitly states that no person — even those who use a pseudonym or those who obtained judicial authority to use an alias — shall execute any public or private document without affixing his or her actual name.
Violation of the law entails jail time of up to five years and a fine of P5,000 up to P10,000.

“It is clear that the Vice President, when she took her oath of office, swore under the Constitution that she would uphold all of our laws. This is again a culpable violation of the Constitution,” Chua said.

“Regarding its application to the acknowledgment receipts of confidential funds, it’s something that the impeachment court should answer,” prosecutor Lordan Suan also added in a separate interview with Rappler.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte trial: Confi fund admission may violate anti-alias law

blocks.text: One Supreme Court ruling in 1996 may be relevant to this issue. Ursua vs Court of Appeals says that the use of a fictitious name in a single instance without indication that the person intends to be known by that name does not fall within the prohibition contained in C.A. No. 142 as amended.
Defense lawyer Justine Gular, who publicly offered this fresh theory of their case for the first time, said they will thresh out their arguments when they present their evidence.

Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia, however, objected to what she called an “eleventh hour” admission of their position, since the angle on aliases was not revealed during the pre-trial. – Rappler.com

articles.title: AI cancer cures slowed by chip shortage, says UK's biggest tech boss
articles.summary: The head of chip designer Arm says modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer cannot be done now, but computers are "going to solve it".

blocks.text: The boss of the biggest UK-headquartered tech firm has said that artifical intelligence will find a cure for cancer that humans cannot in our lifetimes.

Rene Haas, chief executive of Cambridge-based chip designer Arm Holdings, said while modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer was currently "too complex" a problem, computers are "going to solve it" in the future.

Haas also told the BBC that AI would lead to widespread humanoid robots in the next five years, but that its current rapid growth was being held up by a shortage of chips needed to build data centres.
However, he was sceptical about the idea chips could be manufactured in the UK in the future.
Arm designs the brains or CPUs of microchips already used in hundreds of billions of phones, cars, smartwatches and gadgets across the globe.
Earlier this summer, the company's peak share price amid the AI boom made it, in cash terms, the most valuable UK-based company in history.

Haas, who stepped down from the board of British pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca in April, told the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast: "AI is going to... find a cure for cancer that today you and I, other humans [could] not in our lifetimes. I believe in our lifetime, AI will help cure cancer.
"Modelling a cell, modelling a human, modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer - it's too complex a problem, not only for humans today, but the computers that run AI.

"However, going forward, as we feed more and more of the models into these computers, and the computers get more sophisticated to run the models, they're going to solve it," said Haas, who also holds a key role in Arm's main owner, the Japan-based Softbank, which has a range of investments in tech including in OpenAI.
Prof Chris Bakal, from the Institute of Cancer Research, London, and CEO of Sentinal4D, said the real question was no longer whether we use AI, it's what we feed it.
He said in labs like his, they are training AI on data generated themselves from patient samples.

"It is not scraped from the internet. It does not need a giant data centre to run. The future of medical AI will not belong to whoever builds the biggest computer. It will belong to whoever has the right measurements.
"That kind of prediction could cut years from the time it takes to develop new treatments. This is where AI delivers real benefit to patients."

In a wide-ranging interview, Haas said the chips Arm designs would fuel self-learning AI robots "in a very large way" in manufacturing, cleaning, security, building bridges, and doing repairs within a decade.

"With artificial intelligence, these robots can see, learn, and essentially be reprogrammed for new tasks. So, in the service industry, the robot that was programmed to make a bed can also learn how to arrange the towels in a room, or clean the dustbins, or whatever you want to go off and do."

Addressing concerns that AI would lead to mass job losses, Haas said while there would be some change for workers, "the estimates of jobs going away and being completely replaced by machines is a bit overstated" and outweighed by new opportunities.
He also said fears over a correction in the remarkable rise in the stock market value of AI companies were overstated, because of the long-term demand for AI.
Arm's power-efficient technology was now being used in half of AI data centres worldwide, he said.

This has led to a significant evolution in its business in recent months, selling its own microchips. Facebook-owner Meta asked Arm to develop the Arm AGI chip and "demand has been off the charts", according to Haas, with more than $2bn worth of demand since it was launched in March.
There have, however, been challenges in the supply of many types of chips, which Haas believes is holding back the roll-out of AI and data centres.
He pointed to plans for massive "multi-gigawatt" data centres in France and the US as well as plans to put them in space.
"We are absolutely in a supply-constrained environment. Can you get enough chips? We need more fabs [chip factories] before we can put a data centre in space."

But he does not believe that manufacturing, currently centralised around Taiwanese giant TSMC, could eventually occur in the UK, despite the government holding talks with the industry about the possibility of bringing parts of the physical chip supply chain over here.

"I don't think it's necessary for the UK to [build] fabs. Fabs are very expensive. They take a lot of specialised workers. They take a lot of natural resources, and there's a pretty broad ecosystem for those."
As the great hope of UK tech for decades, some government ministers have lamented Arm's sale to Japanese investors in 2016 and subsequent partial flotation on New York's Nasdaq rather than in London.
But Haas maintained that half of Arm's employees remain in the UK and said the company was "by far and away the largest employer in Cambridge".

articles.title: Cities in Great Britain most vulnerable to extreme heat revealed
articles.summary:
OS index examines which ‘urban heat islands’ suffer the most – and which cope the best with rising temperatures

Portsmouth, Leicester, Exeter, Bristol and Nottingham will be among the cities…

blocks.text: Portsmouth, Leicester, Exeter, Bristol and Nottingham will be among the cities that warm the most by the end of this century as global heating turns British cities into urban heat islands, according to research.

Analysis from Ordnance Survey (OS) has created a heat vulnerability index for all cities in Great Britain. Portsmouth, which sits on the south coast of England and is home to 208,000 people, is the most vulnerable to extreme heat today and into the future, according to the research from the OS, the Met Office and the data analysis company 4 Earth Intelligence.

Concrete, asphalt, buildings and hard surfaces in cities absorb solar radiation during the day and act like giant radiators, holding on to the heat rather than cooling down at night as in more rural areas. Cities can be up to 10C hotter than surrounding areas.
Areas most at risk of extreme warming are those with the least tree cover, green space and waterways.

blocks.caption: Portsmouth is the most vulnerable to extreme heat today and into the future, according to the research. Photograph: Peter Titmuss/Alamy

blocks.text: This summer was provisionally the UK’s hottest on record, and the research reveals which cities are suffering now from intense urban heat and which will be among the warmest in future.

The research analyses 71 cities granted by royal charter across England, Scotland and Wales but excluding Northern Ireland. The OS heat vulnerability index suggests that by 2040 all 71 cities will reach high heat vulnerability. By the turn of the century, almost two-thirds could reach the most severe level. Those facing the most severe impact by the end of the century are predicted to be Portsmouth, the City of Westminster, Plymouth, Leicester and Exeter, according to the analysis.
Nick Bolton, the chief executive of Ordnance Survey, said: “Cities are where millions of people live, work and spend their everyday lives.

“Extreme and sustained heat can affect people’s health and wellbeing, how comfortable our homes and workplaces are, and put additional pressure on transport, energy and emergency services. Understanding how and where this vulnerability is changing depends on an accurate view of how the country is built, based on trusted authoritative data, which is critical for planners, developers and local authorities preparing for a warmer future.”

Portsmouth is today the most heat-vulnerable city and will remain at the highest level for warming until the end of the century, according to the research. The city of Leicester is projected to show the biggest rise in Britain’s heat vulnerability rankings, climbing from 10th now to fourth by the end of the century, while Exeter and Nottingham also rise into the 10 most vulnerable cities, alongside Bristol and Brighton and Hove by the end of this century.

Leaders in Portsmouth have identified areas including Somerstown, Portsea, Southsea and Fratton as those particularly exposed to urban heat because of their limited green areas and hard surfaces, and noted that areas with less green space overlap with those of deprivation.
The City of London and the City of Westminster areas rank among the most heat-retentive urban environments in the UK.

The City of London records the highest built-environment score and the least effective natural cooling of any city, given the concentration of buildings, roads and hard surfaces as well as limited green space, trees and water. Westminster ranks third for overall heat vulnerability today and second in both future periods behind Portsmouth.

blocks.caption: Tree cover, green space and waterways can help mitigate the effects of global heating. Photograph: Martin Godwin/The Guardian

blocks.text: A study commissioned by the mayor of London has put the total economic cost of the 2022 London heatwaves at £1.5bn, including productivity losses, health impacts, education disruption, energy demand, transport and emergency services.

The OS heat vulnerability index combined current observed temperatures with the structural characteristics of Britain’s built environment and climate projections into the future to produce a score for every city on a scale of 1 to 5, where 3 to 4 is high and 4 to 5 is severe.

Among cities coping the best with the changing climate is Milton Keynes, which ranks 69th out of 71 cities for heat vulnerability today. Milton Keynes has the lowest built-environment vulnerability in England and the most effective natural cooling of any city in the analysis, with 46 sq km of natural surfaces, against almost 40 sq km of hard made surfaces.

Jonathan Hendry, the chief executive of 4 Earth Intelligence, said exposure varied street by street within a single city. “The areas consistently subjected to higher temperatures than their surroundings are the ones that overheat first during a heatwave,” he said.

“We’re mapping how to turn thermal threats into actionable blueprints for urban resilience, supporting decisions on where heat refuges are sited and how emergency responses are planned in advance rather than in the middle of climate events.”

articles.title: NBI probes P1.9B Davao flood control projects given to just 1 contractor
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has conducted an investigation into the P1.9 billion flood control projects in the district of Davao City Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has conducted an investigation into the P1.9 billion flood control projects in the district of Davao City Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte, which were found to have been awarded to only one contractor, Director Melvin Matibag said.

According to Matibag, the bureau discovered from the Department of Public Works and Highways’ records that P1.9 billion in projects from Duterte’s district were all awarded to Genesis88 Construction, Inc.

“Di ba, ang pinagsimulan nga diyan [flood control scandal], ’yung mga kontraktor na sila na lang ang nakakuha nang nakakuha ng kontrata sa buong Pilipinas. Pero this is a specific area, specific district, na ang nakakuha lang ng kontrata ay yung Genesis 88. Kaya kailangan nating tingnan,” Matibag said in an interview with reporters on Monday.

(What started it [flood control scandal], the contractors were the only ones who got contracts all over the Philippines. But this is a specific area, a specific district, where only Genesis 88 got the contracts. So we have to look at it.)
He mentioned that the NBI’s initial investigation established that the contractor is a “long-time friend” of the Dutertes.
The NBI director also said that records show projects in the district started in 2024 but are still incomplete.
“So, titingnan pa natin. Ebidensya yung tinitingnan natin at hindi ‘marites,’” Matibag said.
(So, we will still look at it. What we are looking at is evidence and not speculation.)
Investigation is still underway
Meanwhile, the NBI director clarified that he is not yet implying that the P1.9 billion flood control projects already have irregularities, noting that the investigation is still underway.

“Kung wala silang kasalanan, then we’re willing to make a statement na tiningnan namin ’yung mga sinasabi na may issue diyan sa flood control at kahit isa lang yung contractor, tapos maayos ang gawa,” Matibag said.

(If they are not guilty, then we’re willing to make a statement that we have looked into the allegations that there is an issue with flood control and even if it was just one contractor, the work was done properly.)

“’Yung investigation is to clear people and to indict people. Kung merong guilty, may ginawang masama, there is a whiff of corruption na naamoy natin, at meron na talaga nangyayaring corruption, kasuhan natin. Pero kung inaakusahan, binabalita, may minamarites, na meron daw mga corruption, at ’yun pa lang, ginawa at tapos naman pala, sabihin din natin,” he added.

(The investigation is to clear people and to indict people. If there is someone guilty, something bad has been done, there is a whiff of corruption that we smell, and there is really corruption going on, let us indict them. But if it is being accused or reported, and there are speculations of corruption, but it turns out the work was done properly, we will also say that.)
‘NBI subpoena vs Duterte, contractor if needed’
When asked if the NBI would issue subpoenas to Duterte and the contractor as its investigation proceeds, Matibag said, “if needed.”
“Kung saan po tayo dadalhin ng ebidensya,” Matibag emphasized.
(Depending on where the evidence will take us.)
“But in the meantime, we’re having a table analysis of the pieces of evidence, documentary evidence that is presented to us,” he said.

In a Facebook post earlier on Monday, Duterte said the NBI must investigate not those who repeatedly win the contracts, but “if there is overpricing, ghost projects, substandard construction, kickbacks, or any theft from the public treasury.”

“Kung may irregularidad man sa pag-award sa proyekto, dapat lang imbestigahan. Pero kung dumaan sa tamang proseso, legal ang award, natapos nang maayos ang proyekto, at walang nakurakot na pera ng bayan, di naman siguro illegal kung sa iilang tao lang na award,” Duterte said.

(If there are irregularities in the awarding of the project, it should be investigated, but if it went through the proper process, the award was legal, the project was completed properly, and no public money was embezzled, then it is probably not illegal if it was awarded to only a few people.)

“Kung may ebidensiya kayo ng krimen, ilabas ninyo at panagutin ang dapat managot. Pero kung wala, tigilan ang trial by publicity at ang pagpaparinig na parang may hatol na bago pa matapos ang imbestigasyon,” the congressman added.

(If you have evidence of a crime, bring it out and hold those responsible accountable. But if not, stop the trial by publicity and making it sound like there is a verdict before the investigation is even finished.) /cb

articles.title: BARMM polls: Over half of Tawi-Tawi bets have ties to political families
articles.summary: Members of political clans, former local officials, civil society leaders and professionals are campaigning for seats in the 80-member Bangsamoro parliament. More than half of them have ties to local…

blocks.text: Members of political clans, former local officials, civil society leaders and professionals are campaigning for seats in the 80-member Bangsamoro parliament. More than half of them have ties to local political families.

items: Political dynasties in Tawi-Tawi are aiming to influence the parliamentary elections for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, with many candidates having ties to local political families.

Candidates from various political clans, including the Que, Matba, and Amilbangsa families, are contesting seats across Tawi-Tawi's four parliamentary districts, with significant involvement from former local officials and civil society leaders.
The elections are set for 2026, with 264,192 registered voters in Tawi-Tawi, and notable candidates include Julbert Que, Rhosatina Sulayman Matolo-De Asis, and Michail Ahaja, among others.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CEBU, Philippines – Political dynasties in Tawi-Tawi, an island province in the southwestern Philippines near Sabah, are seeking to extend their influence into the parliamentary government of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), bringing familiar names and political alliances into the first elections for the region’s parliament.

In the province’s four parliamentary districts, members of political clans, former local officials, civil society leaders and professionals are campaigning for seats in the 80-member Bangsamoro parliament. More than half of them have ties to local political families.

In the first district, one of three Que brothers from Bongao is seeking a parliamentary seat. The Matba, Amilbangsa, Matolo, Jamalul and Ahaja clans also have members in the races for the second, third and fourth districts.
Tawi-Tawi Governor Yshmael Sali’s sister-in-law, Rhosatina Sulayman Matolo-De Asis, is among those seeking a seat in the third district.
Commission on Elections (Comelec) data as of May 8 show that Tawi-Tawi’s 11 towns have 264,192 registered voters for the 2026 BARMM elections.
Here are the candidates running in each of Tawi-Tawi’s four parliamentary districts:

blocks.caption: TAWI-TAWI 1ST DISTRICT RACE. From left: Julbert Que and Shirmal Hajim Sabal. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The first parliamentary district covers Bongao, where the Que family has established a political base. Jasper Que is the mayor of Bongao, while his brother Jimuel is the vice mayor.
Their brother Julbert, a former vice mayor of Bongao, is seeking the parliamentary seat in the first district.
Julbert is the candidate of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), founded by BARMM Member of Parliament Tomanda Antok and led by regional interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua.

He is running against educator Shirmal Hajim Sabal, the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) candidate. The UBJP is the political party of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), led by former BARMM interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim.
Sabal previously served as a provincial director of the BARMM Ministry of Science and Technology.

blocks.caption: TAWI-TAWI 2ND DISTRICT RACE. From left: Abdelaziz Halun, Gamal Hayudini, and Hadjimar Matba. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The second district includes the municipalities of Languyan, South Ubian and Panglima Sugala.
Former South Ubian vice mayor Abdelaziz Halun is in the race under the UBJP. He is up against Gamal Hayudini and Hadjimar Matba.
Hayudini, a retired Philippine Air Force colonel and head of the civil society organization Ako Sama, is the candidate of the BARMM Grand Coalition (BGC).
The BGC is an alliance of the Bangsamoro Peoples Party (BPP), Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo (SIAP), and Al-Ittihad-Ungaya sa Kawagib Nu Bangsamoro.
Matba, a former vice mayor of Languyan and former provincial administrator of Tawi-Tawi, is the candidate of BARMM Member of Parliament Don Mustapha Loong’s Progresibong Bangsamoro Party (PRO BM).
Matba is a relative of incumbent South Ubian Mayor Hadzri Matba.

blocks.caption: TAWI-TAWI 3RD DISTRICT RACE. From left: Mali Albrinji, Dayang Amilbangsa, Alnahada Dalagan, and Rhosatina Sulayman Matolo-De Asis. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The third district comprises the towns of Tandubas, Sapa-Sapa and Simunul.

Mali Albrinji is campaigning under the BGC. He is a former deputy regional manager of the Bangsamoro Ports Management Authority and former regional director of the Maritime Industry Authority under the now-defunct Department of Transportation and Communications in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
Rajsidana Kimble Amilbangsa, a nurse and member of the Amilbangsa clan, is running under the UBJP.
The BFP has fielded Rhosatina Sulayman Matolo-De Asis, a pharmacist and former municipal administrator of Sapa-Sapa.

She is in a race where her political connections are difficult to separate from the contest itself. She is the daughter of former Sapa-Sapa mayor Putli Aisa Sulayman Matolo and sister of Sapa-Sapa Mayor Rhodesia Matolo, who is married to Tawi-Tawi Governor Yshmael Sali.
Meanwhile, the Bangsamoro Party (BAPA), led by BARMM Minister of Labor and Employment Muslimin Sema, has fielded former Tandubas municipal councilor Alnahada Dalagan.
Dalagan is the daughter of the late Roxas Salih, a former mayor of Tandubas and the first chairman of the Tawi-Tawi State Revolutionary Committee of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).

blocks.caption: TAWI-TAWI 4TH DISTRICT RACE. From left: Michail Ahaja, Nur-Mahadil Ahaja, Sanya Jamalul, and Hamdan Kasim. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: Tawi-Tawi Provincial Board Member Michail Ahaja is seeking the parliamentary seat in the fourth district, which comprises the towns of Mapun, Sitangkai, Sibutu and Turtle Islands. The former Tawi-Tawi vice governor and vice mayor of Sitangkai is running as an independent candidate.
Also from the Ahaja political clan is BFP candidate Nur-Mahadil Ahaja, who served as a member of the Bangsamoro parliament from 2019 to 2022.
Sanya Jamalul, daughter of Turtle Islands Mayor Jay Sayang Jamalul and Vice Mayor Mohammad Faisal Jamalul, is an independent candidate for the district seat.
Mapun native Hamdan Musa Kasim is also running under the UBJP in the fourth district. – Rappler.com

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial (September 8, 2026)
articles.summary: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte continues on Tuesday, September 8, 2026. Here are the latest news and updates.

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 6:52am
The Senate impeachment court in session for the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Sept. 7, 2026. Wendell Alinea/Senate Social Media Unit
Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 23: What to expect
A new set of prosecution witnesses is lined up for Tuesday to testify on Article 1 of the impeachment case regarding the alleged misuse of confidential funds by Vice President Sara Duterte.

According to impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol, the House prosecution panel is scheduled to present first this morning Police Major Jovelyn Magay to answer questions on how the information on the acknowledgement receipts of the confidential funds was written.

“‘Yung PNP question document examiner na ipi-presenta ng House prosecution panel, ang balak na patunayan po ng House prosecution panel… ‘yung pagsulat ng mga pangalan doon sa ARs na ‘yun are done by either one person or two or just a few persons na magkakapareho ‘yung strokes, etc.,” Tongol said in a press conference on Monday.

(With the PNP question document examiner who will be presented, the House prosecution panel intends to prove that the writing of names on the ARs was done by either one, two, or just a few persons with similar strokes, etc.)
“‘Yun ‘yung ina-anticipate po na purpose po nung mag-presinta kay PNP Document Examiner Magay tomorrow,” he added.
(That’s the anticipated purpose when PNP Document Examiner Magay is presented tomorrow.)
With this, Tongol explained that the prosecution maintains that the names listed as payees in the ARs are fictitious people, while the defense is trying to prove that they are aliases.

Should the direct, cross, redirect, and recross examinations of Magay, as well as the interjections of senator-judges, be finished within the day, the Senate impeachment court will call the next person to the witness stand.

Based on the impeachment court’s list, Tongol said the next witness lined up after Magay is Sunshine Fajarda, former Assistant Secretary of the Department of Education (DepEd) and incumbent Director VI of the Office of the Vice President (OVP).

Commission on Audit- Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) Assistant Commissioner and Chief Executive Staff Bresilio Sabaldan has also been ordered to testify in the trial. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Habagat’ to bring rains over parts of Luzon, Visayas on Sept. 8
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The southwest monsoon or “habagat” will continue to bring rains over parts of Luzon and Visayas on Tuesday, Sept. 8, with more areas being affected by the weather system in the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The southwest monsoon or “habagat” will continue to bring rains over parts of Luzon and Visayas on Tuesday, with more areas being affected by the weather system in the next few days, according to the state weather bureau.

In the 5 a.m. weather forecast of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), weather specialist Veronica Torres said that no tropical cyclone is being monitored inside and near the Philippine area of responsibility. However, she noted that the possibility of a low-pressure area formation is not being ruled out.
“Asahan natin yung monsoon rains sa Zambales at Bataan. Kapag monsoon rains, ito yung halos tuloy-tuloy na moderate to heavy rains,” Torres said.
(Expect monsoon rains over Zambales and Bataan. Monsoon rains are the continuous moderate to heavy rains.)

Based on the 24-hour rainfall forecast, Zambales and Bataan will experience 100 to 200 millimeters (mm) of rainfall, where numerous flooding events are likely, especially in areas that are urbanized, low-lying, or near rivers. Landslides are also possible in highly susceptible areas.
Occasional rains will prevail over Pampanga, Pangasinan, Tarlac, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro. They will experience 50 to 100 mm of rainfall on Tuesday.
On the other hand, Metro Manila and the rest of Luzon will see cloudy skies and scattered rain showers and thunderstorms.

“Sa susunod na araw, posibleng makaapekto yung habagat sa malaking bahagi ng Luzon. Malaking area yung uulanin, pero pagdating ng Sabado, posibleng mas kumonti yung areas affected by southwest monsoon na magpapaulan sa mga lugar na iyon,” Torres added.
(In the next few days, habagat may possibly affect a huge portion of Luzon. A huge portion will experience rains but less areas may be affected by habagat on Saturday.)
The weather specialist said that rains will continue to persist over Western Visayas while the rest of Visayas and Mindanao will see slightly cloudy to cloudy skies with chances of thunderstorms.
No gale warning is raised in any seaboard of the country.

articles.title: Flight recorders recovered from 'devastating' Amazon cargo plane crash
articles.summary: Five people were killed and five others seriously injured when the Boeing 767-300 overshot the runway at Miami International Airport.

blocks.text: Investigators have recovered the flight recorders from the Amazon cargo plane that crashed at Miami International Airport, but the priority remains the recovery of victims, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has said.
Five people were killed and five others seriously injured when the Boeing 767-300, operated by 21 Air, overshot the runway shortly before 14:00 local time (19:00 BST) on Sunday.
The plane hit two vehicles, including a white van carrying seven people within the airport perimeter, and a Toyota with three passengers.
NTSB chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said it was too early to draw conclusions about what caused the crash, with investigators still in the "fact finding stage".

Speaking at a press conference at Miami International Airport on Monday, Homendy said the aircraft had two crew members on board and was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico, on its third flight of the day.
The plane struck navigational aids and equipment after overrunning the runway, before hitting a white Ford van owned by a contract cleaning company.
It then travelled through a perimeter fence and collided with a Toyota Corolla, coming to rest about 1,300ft (394m) beyond the runway.
Homendy described the crash scene as "devastating", with debris from the aircraft, vehicles and airport fencing scattered across the area.
"It's hard to see, and I'm sure very difficult for the first responders as well," she said.
She said recovering victims' bodies was the current priority, adding: "The investigation and access to the aircraft, as well as evidence, can wait."
The flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder have been recovered and are being sent to NTSB headquarters for evaluation.
Homendy said investigators could not yet say anything substantive about the cause of the crash as they were still collecting evidence at the scene.

Investigators will examine the flight history, crew experience and training, radar data, and aircraft performance. Separate teams will look at the plane's systems and engines, while a meteorologist will assess the weather conditions at the time of landing.

The NTSB will also examine whether the runway should have had an engineered materials arresting system (EMAS), which is designed to slow and stop aircraft that overrun a runway. Homendy said this would be a "key" part of the investigation.
Earlier analysis by BBC Verify found there was an active thunderstorm near the airport shortly before the crash, with winds gusting up to 26 knots.
The NTSB has appealed for members of the public to share photographs or videos that could aid the investigation.
Homendy said the agency would make safety recommendations at the end of its investigation. "That's why we're here - to prevent the next tragedy," she said.
"Our recommendations must be implemented, or we'll be here again."

Two of the four runways at the airport remained closed following the crash. Passengers have been warned to expect further disruption after Sunday's cancellations affected the arrival of aircraft and flight crews.
The crash happened during the Labor Day holiday weekend, one of the busiest travel periods in the US.
Amazon said it was "heartbroken" by the loss of life and that it was working closely with authorities.
21 Air, the company operating the aircraft, expressed its condolences and said it was co-operating with the investigation.

articles.title: Eiffel Tower employees strike after female staff removed
articles.summary: The employees protested against the removal of the site's female workers due to a request by a visiting Hindu group. The tower's operating company apologized for the decision.

image.caption: The Eiffel Tower was closed for visits on Monday due to the strikeImage: Sarah Meyssonnier/REUTERS

blocks.text: The Eiffel Tower in Paris, France, was closed on Monday after staff went on strike to protest the exclusion of female workers during a visit by a Hindu religious group.
Visitors to the tower on Monday saw a message that says its opening is "delayed for operational reasons."

The staff released a statement in which they condemned "professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex" during the religious group's visit.
Around 100 men from the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) spiritual movement were visiting the landmark.
The company that operates the Tower, SETE, said that the group had requested a visit as part of which the "interactions with women" would be limited.
Emmanuel Gregoire, Paris' Socialist mayor, called the incident "unacceptable."
"Equality between women and men will never end at the foot of our historic monuments, nor anywhere else in this city," Gregoire said.

blocks.caption: The entrance to the Eiffel Tower was 'delayed for operational reasons' the signs readImage: Sarah Meyssonnier/REUTERS

blocks.text: Eiffel Tower operator regrets incident
SETE accepted that the decision was a mistake.
"These conditions should not have been accepted," SETE said.
Company head Ariel Weil told the AFP news agency that SETE will "draw the necessary conclusions" from the case. Weil himself is an elected official in Paris.
"No motive of a religious order could justify a distinction based on gender or any other discriminatory consideration in welcoming the public," Weil wrote on his X account.
The Eiffel Tower sees some seven million visitors a year. It was closed all day due to the strike, but will open again on Tuesday, a staff representative said.

articles.title: Illinois mother charged with killing toddler 'invested' in Lindsay Clancy case: prosecutors
articles.summary: An Illinois woman charged with killing her two-year-old son had been closely following the murder trial of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy and was texting friends about the case just hours before…

image.caption: Police in Illinois have charged a woman with first-degree murder after her two-year-old son was found dead in the basement of the family's suburban Chicago home on Sept. 1. (Matt Rourke/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

An Illinois woman charged with killing her two-year-old son had been closely following the murder trial of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy and was texting friends about the case just hours before her son was found dead, prosecutors said.
Prosecutors allege Corie Walsh texted friends about trial hours before son found dead

Corie Walsh, 40, was charged with three counts of first-degree murder after her son, Barrett, was found dead in the basement of the family's suburban Chicago home on Sept. 1, according to court records obtained by NBC Chicago.

Prosecutors said Walsh had become "very invested" in Clancy's nationally watched trial and was discussing it with friends until about 12:30 p.m. that day. A neighbour found Barrett less than four hours later.

Walsh was found elsewhere in the home with injuries that authorities said were self-inflicted. Prosecutors said she later told investigators that she killed her son because she believed he was the "devil" and the "anti-Christ." Her lawyer, Andrea Lyon, told reporters Walsh was experiencing a psychotic episode and called the boy's death a tragedy for the entire family.

Police were called to Walsh's home in Frankfort, about 56 kilometres southwest of Chicago, shortly before 4 p.m. after a neighbour discovered Barrett in the basement, according to prosecutors' petition seeking to keep Walsh jailed before trial.
Mistrial declared over deadlocked jury in Lindsay Clancy case

The neighbour found the boy and began CPR while calling 911, prosecutors said. He was taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. An autopsy determined that he died from asphyxia caused by ligature compression of the neck.

Police searching the house found Walsh fully dressed in a bathtub containing bloody water, prosecutors said. She had cuts to her wrists and thighs and was taken to a hospital with injuries authorities described as not life-threatening.

The disclosure that Walsh had been following Clancy's trial came days after a Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in that case on Friday, when jurors said they could not reach a unanimous verdict.

items: Will Lindsay Clancy face a new trial? What's next after mistrial declared

blocks.text: Clancy, a former labour and delivery nurse, was accused of killing her three young children in 2023. Her lawyers argued that she was legally insane and suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors maintained that Clancy understood what she was doing and knew it was wrong.

Authorities in Illinois have not alleged that Clancy's trial played a role in the killing of Walsh's son, and no evidence made public so far establishes a connection beyond her discussion of the case.
Frankfort police and prosecutors in Will County did not respond to calls for comment on Monday.

articles.title: NSW Greens MP pleads with federal colleagues not to back National party motion to block koala park deal
articles.summary:
Federal Greens partyroom split over plan for NSW to get millions of dollars worth in carbon credits for creating a koala national park

A New South Wales Greens MP has made an impassioned…

blocks.text: A New South Wales Greens MP has made an impassioned plea to her federal colleagues, urging them not to vote with the Coalition and One Nation to block a plan for the NSW government to get millions of dollars’ worth in carbon credits for creating a koala national park.

Sue Higginson, a former lawyer and forest campaigner turned NSW upper house MP, is the first member of the minor party to speak in detail about a dispute that has split the Greens and environmentalists.
The disagreement is over a federal regulation, known as a carbon credit method, that allows state governments that protect native forests on public land to earn credits from logging.
The Nationals want to kill the regulation on behalf of the forestry industry through a disallowance motion and a Senate vote is scheduled next week.
The federal Greens will discuss on Tuesday whether to back the pro-logging Nationals’ motion on the grounds the koala park should be created, but not this way.
Among their considerations will be the political fallout for the environmental party if it is accused of standing in the way of a nature protection. None have spoken publicly on the issue.

The meeting follows weeks of lobbying by conservationists, including in full-page newspaper advertisements and email drives. The Australia Institute, which wants the method killed, has declared the issue the “first big climate test” of Larissa Waters’s leadership of the party.

Each Australian carbon credit is said to represent one tonne of greenhouse gas emissions that has been prevented from being released or drawn down from the atmosphere. Their use is contentious, partly because polluting companies can buy an unlimited number of credits – also known as offsets – to count as their own cuts while continuing to pollute.

Peer-reviewed studies have found some existing carbon credit methods have not effectively reduced emissions and scientists say limiting the climate crisis requires rapid direct emissions cuts and offsets should be used sparingly.

Those who want the regulation killed, including the Bob Brown Foundation and the Wilderness Society, say NSW Labor proposed a koala park near Coffs Harbour a decade before announcing it was dependent on carbon credit revenue, and the offsets created would not represent real emissions reductions. They say the method sets a precedent for other state governments to withhold environment protection unless they get carbon credits.

On the other side are NSW conservation and Indigenous groups, national groups including WWF, Greenpeace and the Ken Henry-led Australian Climate and Biodiversity Foundation, and some senior ecologists. They say there is no guarantee the park would go ahead as promised if the method was disallowed, and that critics are too dismissive of what protecting 176,000 hectares of additional forests home to more than 100 threatened species would mean for forests that have been devastated by decades of logging and how hard local campaigners have fought over decades for this win.

Higginson told the Guardian she found the idea of carbon credits from protecting public forests “offensive” and initially opposed what is known as the “improved native forestry method”. Her thinking after the design was strengthened during development to force a substantial reduction in logging across NSW forests that was not part of NSW premier Chris Minns’ initial commitment.

“The numbers that matter most in this fight are how many hectares of forest can we save, how big can we make our national park estate, how many First Nations’ people we can get working on country, how much carbon can we draw down and sequester in our forests as they grow big old, how many fires we can protect our forests from, how many greater gliders, forests owls, swift parrots and koalas we can save and how much can we make climate polluters pay to charge them out of existence,” she said.

Higginson said forestry industry leaders planned a separate, less environmentally friendly carbon credit method that could be adopted if the current method failed. She said the industry proposal would “lock in native forest logging for many more years and see the generation of carbon credits of far less integrity”.

“This is about winning the forests,” she said. “If our fight is about destroying carbon credits, let’s do that. Let’s tear down the entire system together. [But] the National party’s disallowance will do the opposite of that.”

Higginson’s position is broadly backed by some independent senators, including David Pocock and the former Green Lidia Thorpe. But it puts her on the opposite side of the issue to her mentor, and the person who asked her to run for parliament, the former Australian Greens leader Bob Brown.

Higginson said she was “devastated” when she learned their policy split over the issue given Brown’s legacy, but they continue to campaign together, including at an event for Sydney’s southern forests on Saturday.

Brown said he understood the desperation of “very good people” who believed they had no option other than to support the method, but said Minns had broken an election promise and joined Anthony Albanese in “putting capitalism before the environment”.

He said Australia had created about 600 national parks, none before had needed carbon credit revenue and the method would be “letting polluters off the hook”. “It’s absolutely the wrong thing to do,” he said. “My view is if the disallowance motion goes through [Minns] would have to go back to his initial position to protect the park.”
He called on Greens senators “not to be coerced by Labor’s anti-environmental gimmick”. But he said he would still support them if they ultimately disagreed. “Labor is the villain here,” he said.

articles.title: Minors, the dead ‘received’ secret funds from OVP, DepEd
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Two 1-year-old babies were listed as receiving P400,000 each from Vice President Sara Duterte’s confidential funds. At least 23 other minors and 37 people whose names matched…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Two 1-year-old babies were listed as receiving P400,000 each from Vice President Sara Duterte’s confidential funds. At least 23 other minors and 37 people whose names matched death records also appeared among the supposed payees, according to Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) records presented at the impeachment trial on Monday.

The findings involved 2,669 supposed recipients from the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd), with 1,685—or 63 percent—having no birth, marriage or death records in the PSA’s Civil Registry System.
Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia said the records would help establish that confidential funds were liquidated under the names of nonexistent, deceased persons and children.

The testimony of PSA Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande drew scrutiny from senator-judges, who questioned whether the names represented real people, aliases or identities that could not be established.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva asked Grande to characterize the 63-percent figure.
“Unusual,” she replied, noting that only about 7 percent to 8 percent of names typically produce negative results in other verifications.
The most striking matches involved children. Grande said 20 names on the OVP list and five on the DepEd list matched minors’ birth records.

An acknowledgment receipt showed Miko Alquizar supposedly received P400,000 on March 28, 2023. His birth record showed he was born on June 11, 2022, making him about a year old when the payment was recorded.
Beatrice Cuenca was listed as receiving P400,000 on March 13, 2023. Her birth record showed she was born on Jan. 7, 2022.
Mikay delos Reyes was listed as receiving P200,000 on March 27, 2023. Her birth record showed she was born on Jan. 13, 2020, making her 3 years old.
Asked for the youngest person whose name matched a PSA record, Grande identified Marlin Sunga, whose record showed she was 2 months old.
Then came the catch: Sunga was born in 1965 and died on Nov. 2 of the same year.
Receipts bearing the names Fortunato Salig, Emilio Sagan and Rodolfo Traya also matched death certificates, Grande said.

But Grande cautioned that a name match did not necessarily establish that the person named on the receipt was already dead when the payment was made. It meant only that the name matched that of a person in PSA records.
She repeatedly stressed that she was testifying only on the availability of civil registry records, not on whether the people named in the documents actually existed.
Then came the aliases
The defense abruptly changed the complexion of the testimony by declaring that the unusual names were aliases.
“Given that it has become a material matter, we have to couch this answer that this is classified information, but these are, in fact, aliases,” defense lawyer Justin Gular told the court.
It was the first time Duterte’s defense team acknowledged the unusual names as aliases.
Divinagracia objected, saying it was “a tad too late” for the defense to take that position after the prosecution had subjected the names to PSA verification.
Gular countered that the Commission on Audit had not flagged the names or alleged use of aliases as a problem and that the prosecution still had the burden of proof.
Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison said the defense was not required to reveal its evidence or theory while the prosecution was still presenting its case.
Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero agreed, saying he could not force the defense to present evidence or disclose its theory.
Among the other names that drew attention were Timon Angelo Pusa, Tomas Panda, Xioame Ocho, Dan Rick Otso, Arthur Baon, Beverly Claire Pampano, Mathew Keso, Charles Sampaloc Jr. and Maxine Callos.
Grande said she personally rechecked some of the names because they appeared unusual or unique.
Name not an identity
Villanueva asked how the PSA could verify people who might have used aliases.
Grande said the agency would need a person’s real name to establish an identity.
Senator-judge Sherwin Gatchalian likewise questioned whether the PSA findings could establish that the listed individuals actually existed.
Grande said the PSA had conducted further verification but had not investigated their actual existence.
She nevertheless said the probability of a person having no birth, marriage or death record was “extremely slim.”
Senator-judge Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino IV said the distinction between aliases and real identities was crucial.
“If these are aliases, then that’s a different matter,” Aquino said, noting that an alias would naturally not appear in the PSA database.

He said only former OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta had previously described the names as aliases and that the court should determine whether they represented aliases or real people whose identities could be found in other government records.
Grande said the 2020 census showed that 96.6 percent of Filipinos had registered births, while unofficial 2024 figures put birth registration at about 97 percent to 97.1 percent.

Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro later said in a press briefing that the prosecution was less concerned about the use of aliases or unusual names than about how the confidential funds were used and liquidated, and whether the OVP and DepEd complied with Joint Circular No. 2015-01.
Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo raised another red flag: the apparent similarity of handwriting and signatures on receipts carrying different names.
Tulfo said aliases could be justified to protect intelligence informants, but questioned why supposedly different informants appeared to have the same handwriting and signatures.
“The signatures were identical, and the handwriting was the same across different names,” Tulfo said, calling the documents “very questionable.” —WITH REPORTS FROM ISABELLE PECHAY, AND KEITH CLORES

articles.title: VP: Ex-AFP chief assured my family protection
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday said that in 2024, then Armed Forces of the Philippines chief of staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. assured her that her children and mother…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday said that in 2024, then Armed Forces of the Philippines chief of staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. assured her that her children and mother would be spared from being dragged into any government action against her.
Duterte made the statement after releasing a screenshot of what she described as a private message exchange with Brawner dated Feb. 7, 2024.

“Since my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it appropriate to convey certain important requests to former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner [Jr.],” she said.
“Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or intimidated by whatever might be done to me,” she added.
In the screenshot, Brawner purportedly assured Duterte that President Marcos “will not allow anything to happen” to her and to her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte.

Brawner also supposedly told Duterte that he would inform her as soon as he learned of any arrest order against her, and that if any action were to be taken against her, it would be carried out “outside [the Vice President’s] residence.”
Duterte, for her part, responded that she was “not worried” and was simply going through what was in her “task list.”
“As for the important No. 2 matter—just not where my children and my mother are. Just tell everyone to look for me outside,” she said.
In her statement, Duterte stressed that the act of authorities going to or even just approaching the location where both her children and her mother were “is a serious matter.”
“Especially when minors are involved or affected. Children should not be used, intimidated, or dragged into acts of harassment or coercion. This constitutes child abuse,” she said.
Duterte first mentioned her children being affected by her legal troubles on Saturday, when she appeared in court to post bail for the three counts of grave threats filed against her.
Coordinated effort
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla disputed Duterte’s claims, stating that arresting authorities did not even enter her residence’s interior, nor was there a commotion resulting from their presence.

“Never did we enter the house to harass her mother or her children. The police are there every night [outside her house] just to provide deterrence if someone wants to attack the Vice President. That’s SOP,” Remulla said at a press briefing in Camp Crame.

“Child abuse is a serious charge… There was no SWAT (Special Weapons and Tactics team). There was no armed component. The women (police) were all unarmed. They were duly accepted into their residence and into their office,” Remulla said.

Duterte had also claimed harassment by the police related to her arrest warrant. But Remulla said police knowledge of Duterte’s whereabouts, which was needed to serve the warrant, was “not a cloak-and-dagger affair” but a coordinated effort between her security team and the police, one that “involved direct communication between the two parties.”

“So, any thoughts of harassment during the service [are] totally untrue. We dare them to present any CCTV [footage] that they have in their office, in their residence, of harassment that went on in the service of the warrant,” said Remulla.
No supporting evidence

Meanwhile, Malacañang on Monday pushed back at Duterte’s statements that she had received information in 2024 about alleged plans by President Marcos to “attack” her and secure an International Criminal Court warrant against former President Duterte.
At a briefing, Palace press officer Claire Castro denied Duterte’s claims, saying they were baseless.
“We categorically deny this allegation made by the Vice President. There is no evidence to support it, nor are there any records that can substantiate this claim,” said Castro.
The Palace also distanced itself from what some quarters decried as the red-carpet treatment given to Duterte at the Quezon City Hall of Justice over the weekend.

Duterte arrived at the Hall of Justice on Saturday to post bail, following the arrest warrant issued against her for her alleged threats against the President, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Photos and videos showed a red carpet being rolled out for Duterte as she entered the building, raising questions among some observers as to why such treatment was given to an individual facing an arrest warrant.
But according to Castro, “we cannot say what the court’s reason was for putting up the red carpet. That is no longer within the scope of the executive branch.”

Duterte posted bail for each of the three counts of grave threats filed against her before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC). In total, her cash bond amounted to P360,000, or P120,000 for each of the three counts.
Duterte appeared in person before RTC Branch 98 accompanied by her lawyers, Paul Lawrence Lim and Michael Poa. —WITH REPORTS FROM DEXTER CABALZA, AND LUISA CABATO

articles.title: Legarda extends leave for fifth time
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda has extended her medical leave for the fifth time, keeping her away from the Senate until Sept. 16. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, meanwhile, stepped up his…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda has extended her medical leave for the fifth time, keeping her away from the Senate until Sept. 16.

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, meanwhile, stepped up his criticism of the senator’s prolonged absence amid a preliminary investigation into alleged P10.44-billion irregularities involving solar power projects.
Senate Secretary Renato Bantug on Monday confirmed that Legarda would be on extended leave.
“Yes. For Sept. 7-9 and [Sept.] 14-16,” Bantug said in a text message when asked if the senator had filed another extension.

Legarda first filed medical leave from Aug. 3 to 5 and has since repeatedly sought extensions, mostly covering Mondays to Wednesdays, the days set by the Senate impeachment court for the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Senate leaders have said she is undergoing treatment for a serious lung-related illness. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri and Sen. Panfilo Lacson have separately said Legarda is being treated for a lung problem.
Legarda has not publicly disclosed details of her condition.
‘May not return’
At a press conference on Monday, Remulla suggested that Legarda and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, might not return to the Philippines, saying they appeared to be avoiding accountability.
“They probably won’t come back because it seems like they’re avoiding paying for what they did,” Remulla said in Filipino.
He described the two as “running away and hiding somewhere else,” and said the Ombudsman would continue pursuing the case.
Remulla said he would travel to France on Friday to coordinate with French authorities, amid information that Legarda, Leviste and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co were in that country.
“We will make the world smaller,” he said in Filipino, adding that France should not become a refuge for people accused of stealing public wealth.

Remulla said his office has been considering measures to ensure that Legarda and Leviste remain available to face investigation, including possible moves involving their passports, as the agency continues its preliminary probe.
Leave under scrutiny
Remulla’s remarks came as Legarda’s repeated medical leave extensions continued to draw scrutiny.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano earlier described the extensions as “quite suspicious,” noting that they coincided with its preliminary investigation into complaints of plunder and graft against Legarda, Leviste and former Energy Secretary Alfonso Cusi.

The investigation concerns allegations that Leviste’s renewable energy company failed to deliver solar power commitments under its congressional franchise, resulting in billions of pesos in alleged unpaid obligations.
Remulla has said Legarda was included because she was Senate finance committee chair when the franchise was secured.

Records from the National Bureau of Investigation showed that Legarda left for France on Aug. 2, a day before her initial medical leave took effect. Her son separately left the country on the same day.

Legarda has rejected the allegations as false and baseless and previously said she had complied with Senate rules in filing her medical leave. She has also maintained that no public funds were involved. /cb

articles.title: Tacloban school shooting survivor needs help for another surgery
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — Nearly three months after surviving the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School (SJNHS) here, 17-year-old Joan Viñas continues to battle the physical and…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — Nearly three months after surviving the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School (SJNHS) here, 17-year-old Joan Viñas continues to battle the physical and emotional wounds left by the tragedy as she prepares for another surgery this week.
Joan is scheduled to undergo a cranioplasty at the Eastern Visayas Medical Center (EVMC) in this city, and her family needs at least P40,000 to cover the procedure’s cost.
Her mother, Rowena, is appealing for financial assistance, saying the family has already received government and other aid but still lacks money to cover Joan’s continuing medical needs.
“We are appealing for financial assistance as Joan will undergo another surgery,” Rowena told the Inquirer on Monday.

Joan, a Grade 10 student, was among the three students seriously injured when a 14-year-old student, identified as “Nash,” went on a shooting rampage inside the school on June 22. Three students were killed in the attack while 20 others were either wounded or injured.
Joan had a bullet wound in the head. The bullet struck her head and exited through her right eye, leaving her with a serious eye injury and the need for continuing medical treatment.
She was confined at EVMC for 12 days following the shooting.
Eye injury
Joan is scheduled to undergo another surgery in November to address the injury to her right eye and hopefully restore her eyesight.
The timing of the second surgery is particularly significant for Joan, as it is scheduled around her 18th birthday.

Rowena said the family had received assistance from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) through Tingog party list and from several individuals and groups who helped Joan during her hospitalization.
However, the assistance received so far has not been enough to meet the expenses for her succeeding surgeries.
Rowena has no regular employment, while her husband, Joseph, works as a job order employee of the Tacloban City government. Joan is the youngest of their eight children.
Despite surviving the shooting, Joan said the incident continues to haunt her.
She recalled that she was inside her classroom when the shooting began. She ran to another classroom to check on her cousin, Yuriza Ay-ay, also in Grade 10, when she was struck by the bullet.
While Joan is grateful to have survived, she said she is still struggling to come to terms with what happened.
When asked about reports that Nash has not been charged in connection with the shooting, Joan became emotional.
“I want him also to be charged. I want him to suffer for what he did to us,” she said.
Nash’s companion, “Rod,” 15, was charged with murder. Both are now under the custody of the DSWD rehabilitation center in Tanauan, Leyte.
The June 22 shooting prompted renewed concerns over security and safety in schools in Eastern Visayas.
The two other students who were seriously injured have since returned to school, Joan has yet to attend her classes at SJNHS as she continues her recovery.
Joan, however, remains hopeful that she will return to school and pursue her dream of becoming a nurse. /cb

articles.title: House panel OKs social media ban for kids
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A House of Representatives panel has proposed a full social media ban for children below 13 and restrictions on the said technology’s use for those aged 13 to 18, as a means to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A House of Representatives panel has proposed a full social media ban for children below 13 and restrictions on the said technology’s use for those aged 13 to 18, as a means to shield young people from harmful content online.

During a hearing of the House committee on the welfare of children, Pasig City Rep. Roman Romulo presented the still unnumbered substitute bill to 10 proposals seeking to protect minors from the dangers of unabated social media use.
According to Romulo, the full ban for children below 13 is meant to restrict them from having any screen time.

“Basically the bill now will be a ban on all social media platforms for those under 13. What we want is for them not to have any screen time,” said Romulo, chair of the House committee on basic education and culture and head of the technical working group that crafted the substitute bill.
Meanwhile, the proposed restrictions for those aged 13 to 18 will cover viewing short videos, using messaging applications, and accessing harmful content.

“For those 13 to below 18 years of age, we will have a ban on features such as harmful content, which is defined in the law [as] topics revolving around violence, sex, and similar topics,” Romulo said.
“Scrolling shorts will be banned, and also chat groups. So if you’re 13 [and above but] below 18, you cannot join chat groups. That is where we are headed,” he added.
Local office requirement

Romulo admitted that the House’s version of the bill is different from what the Senate has passed. Senate Bill No. 2424 or the proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act proposed that 16 be considered the minimum age for social media use. The latter bill was brought to the plenary on Aug. 26 following approval by the Senate committee on public information and mass media.
However, Romulo believes such differences can be sorted out in a bicameral conference committee hearing, should both bills be approved by the respective chambers of Congress.

Romulo said the substitute bill also requires social media companies to “register a Philippine presence” if they want to operate in the country, so that they can be held accountable under Philippine laws.

“If you are to be accessed by any individual or corporation in the Philippines, you must be registered in the Philippines. If we don’t have jurisdiction over that entity, our authority over the platforms is very hollow,” he said.

Romulo said the technical working group purposely left out provisions related to parental consent and limiting screen time for adolescents, as they are matters the House should decide upon during the plenary deliberations, specifically during the period of amendments.
“All members should be heard, as this is an important piece of legislation,” said Romulo.
Violent online content

Calls for a social media ban for children have emerged amid fears that unrestricted online access influenced the students who were behind the shooting incidents at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City on June 22 and Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City on Aug. 18.
Three students were killed during the Tacloban shooting, while two, including the gunman, were confirmed dead after the incident at Ateneo de Zamboanga University.

The perpetrators in both incidents were supposedly exposed to violent content online, or joined groups engaged in nihilistic violent extremist (NVE) behavior or senseless violence. NVE is being looked at as an angle in the two school shooting incidents.

On Aug. 28, Sen. Risa Hontiveros said Philippine authorities have been able to secure a commitment from Meta, which owns and manages the social media sites Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, along with other messaging apps, to provide authorities important information should they spot a possible threat to children. /cb

articles.title: Romualdez arrested in hospital for plunder
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Speaker and incumbent Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez was arrested on Monday for plunder, hours after he and former Ako Bicol Rep. Elizaldy Co were charged before the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Speaker and incumbent Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez was arrested on Monday for plunder, hours after he and former Ako Bicol Rep. Elizaldy Co were charged before the Sandiganbayan over allegations they received more than P7 billion in kickbacks from government projects between 2022 and 2025.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla told reporters that Romualdez was arrested at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City where he is currently confined.
“According to the doctors, he suffered from a cardiovascular event. His blood pressure was unstable and he was having an anxiety attack,” Remulla said.

The lawmaker’s lawyers have asked the Sandiganbayan’s Third Division, which will handle the plunder case against him, Co and their two other coaccused, to let him remain at the hospital after his arrest.
In a motion seeking his continued hospital confinement, Romualdez’s lawyers cited his “documented cardiac history,” diabetes and primary hypothyroidism, among other ailments.

“Accused seeks no exemption from arrest, custody, booking, security restrictions, court appearances or eventual transfer to the detention facility designated by the [court]. The requested accommodation rests exclusively on documented necessity, remains subject to continuous custody and judicial supervision and may be independently verified by a court-designated or government physicians,” they said.

The antigraft court, which also issued a hold departure order for the accused, earlier said the issuance of the arrest warrant signified that after personally evaluating the records, it found “probable cause to believe that [they] committed the offense charged.”

Based on the charge sheet filed by the Office of the Ombudsman earlier in the day before the Sandiganbayan, Romualdez and Co were accused of “repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least fifteen (15) occasions, commissions, shares, percentages, kickbacks, ‘commitments’ and/or other pecuniary benefits” worth at least P7.44 billion.

The amount allegedly came from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects that were funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025.
The P7.44 billion, according to the case information, was “specifically traced and laundered [by] setting up and/or using shell or dummy corporations and conduits.”
Respecting legal process

Aside from Romualdez and Co, also named in the charge sheet were a member of the former Speaker’s staff, Jocelyn Sereño, and a certain Felicito Guevarra, the president of a money changer corporation. It was not immediately clear why they were included in the case.
In a statement, Romualdez’s lawyer and spokesperson Ade Fajardo said his client respects the courts and legal process and will face the allegations against him.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” Fajardo added.

“Representative Romualdez asks for no special treatment. He asks only for the same due process and fair hearing guaranteed to every Filipino. Truth, evidence, and a fair process should prevail,” the lawyer said.
In Malacañang, Palace press officer Claire Castro said she has yet to receive a formal reaction from President Marcos, who is a first cousin of Romualdez.
However, Malacañang respects the Ombudsman’s action as the filing of cases falls within its mandate, she added.
“Whatever the evidence shows should simply be presented before the court,” Castro said, noting that Romualdez and his other coaccused may also present their own evidence to defend themselves.

In his fifth State of the Nation Address (Sona) on July 27, President Marcos acknowledged that his cousin could be arrested and detained as part of his administration’s sweeping campaign against corruption.

“Painful as it may be for us, we have to do what is right,” Marcos said. “I am not the President of my family. I am not the President of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines, and my duty is to you, my fellow Filipinos.”
The President earlier defended what critics had decried as a snail-paced government investigation into the multibillion-peso flood control controversy which he exposed in his 2025 Sona.
Malacañang urged the public not to be impatient, saying that Mr. Marcos was bent on keeping his promise of catching the “big fishes” in the corruption scandal.
‘Not easy’
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla likewise addressed the issue in a press briefing shortly after the filing of the case, saying they did not want to submit “a case that is still raw.”
“We want the evidence to be there already. That’s what we did here, the process was not easy,” he told reporters.
Remulla said that more cases would be eventually filed against Romualdez.
“It’s a series of cases, not just this, there are many more cases to be filed besides plunder. There are other plunder cases and money laundering cases,” he added.

Remulla also clarified that prosecutors have yet to use the evidence provided by former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan, who was discharged last week from his plunder and graft cases after he became a state witness.

Romualdez was earlier accused of facilitating budget insertions during his term as Speaker under the 19th and 20th Congress to implement allegedly anomalous infrastructure programs and for supposedly receiving kickbacks from these projects.

However, he and his legal team have insisted that he was not involved in any wrongdoing, maintaining repeatedly that despite being the House’s top leader, he did not have control over every step of the budget-making process in Congress.

Romualdez eventually stepped down as Speaker in September last year after he and other lawmakers were named by contractor couple Pacifico “Curlee” Discaya II and Cezarah “Sarah” Discaya as alleged recipients of kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.

According to Romualdez, he wanted to stop the chamber’s “bleeding credibility” following allegations linking him and other lawmakers to questionable public works projects. —WITH REPORTS FROM DEXTER CABALZA, AND INQUIRER RESEARCH

articles.title: Angara: Can’t hire teachers with ‘zero’ allocation
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) won’t be able to hire more than 14,000 new teachers next year unless Congress restores its funding request, Secretary Sonny Angara said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) won’t be able to hire more than 14,000 new teachers next year unless Congress restores its funding request, Secretary Sonny Angara said on Monday.

The department was earmarked P973.40 billion under the P7.2-trillion 2027 National Expenditure Program, down from its P1.01-trillion funding this year. Its request for funding for teachers’ recruitment was reduced to zero.

“Unfortunately, there was none,” Angara told lawmakers at the House of Representatives, confirming the Department of Budget and Management’s zero allocation for DepEd’s recruitment program. “But we’re hoping that it will be hiked in the course of the budgetary process.”

The education chief’s presentation showed the agency had requested an additional P49.16 billion from Congress for its “personnel improvement” program, including P4.29 billion for the hiring of 14,274 teachers.
“This is part of the wish list,” he said, pointing out that this year, DepEd recruited 32,000 teachers, way above its annual average of 20,000 hired teachers.
‘Discretionary’
Besides funding for Teacher I posts, Angara also requested P16.64 billion for hiring 39,428 Project Development Officer I staff and P10.52 billion to fund 14,126 School Principal I posts.
A budget watchdog, however, warned that DepEd’s proposed spending plan is becoming “discretionary, centrally pooled.”
In a statement, the Amplify Education Budget Initiative observed that some line items in the proposed budget have been merged, muddling transparency and civil society oversight.

“Vouchers, inclusive-education funds and school-building money that once carried regional shares or stood as their own line items are now pooled in the Central Office, with no published list of what will be built or bought,” it said.
The group warned the agency’s Central Office would hold outsized discretion “over tens of billions of pesos,” a trend it saw as worrying as the nation heads into an election cycle in 2028.
“When the same money is merged into a broad Central Office pool, that trail goes dark, and the choice of who benefits shifts from a transparent formula to an official’s discretion,” it said.
Room for flexibility

Previously separate line items now merged into one include the voucher program for senior high school students in the academic and trade track and the Educational Service Contracting project for junior high school students.
Those initiatives, now consolidated under the Government Assistance and Subsidies program, were earmarked P38.1 billion for next year.
Angara later told reporters the agency was prompted to combine the three programs for budget flexibility. /cb

articles.title: 2 DPWH engineers sacked after man falls to death in canal
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has sacked two of his engineers in Pampanga province’s third district after a man fell to his death in an open drainage canal during monsoon…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has sacked two of his engineers in Pampanga province’s third district after a man fell to his death in an open drainage canal during monsoon rains late last month.

Aser Mallari and Agustin Dagsaan Jr., officers in charge in the Department of Public Works and Highways’ Office of District Engineer and Office of the Assistant District Engineer, respectively, were relieved on Sunday for their “failure to comply with the required safety measures.”
