articles.title: End parliamentary courtesy for OP, OVP budgets – watchdogs
articles.summary: Lawmakers should stop giving the Office of the President and Office of the Vice President a free pass during budget deliberations and subject their spending plans to the same scrutiny as other…

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am

Calls to end the practice of extending “parliamentary courtesy” in the House and Senate come amid concerns over the size of allocations and alleged anomalies involving confidential and intelligence funds (CIF) and the Local Government Support Fund.
Philstar.com / Enrico Alonzo

MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers should stop giving the Office of the President (OP) and Office of the Vice President (OVP) a free pass during budget deliberations and subject their spending plans to the same scrutiny as other agencies, according to budget watchdogs.
Public finance specialist Zy-za Nadine Suzara said this must be abolished as it undermines full budget transparency and accountability.

“Public trust is now very low because of opacity in the many aspects of the budget. It is no longer acceptable to accept parliamentary courtesy for both the OP and OVP in light of both the level of allocations and anomalies surrounding the use of the confidential and intelligence funds,” Suzara told The STAR.

Her remarks came after the House appropriations committee last week swiftly approved the OP’s proposed P10.2-billion budget for 2027, with lawmakers voting 37-5 to end the deliberations after invoking parliamentary courtesy.
The proposed allocation is about 64 percent lower than the OP’s P28-billion budget for 2026.
But Suzara said the OP’s proposed CIF accounts for about half of the total CIF being sought under the 2027 National Expenditure Program.

“On the other hand, the Vice President is on trial for the misuse of her confidential funds. Furthermore, the public deserves to know what other items are funded in the budgets of OP and OVP,” she added.
The OVP proposed a P785.2-million budget for next year, down 11.7 percent from its P889.24-million 2026 allocation.
For University of the Philippines professor and former finance undersecretary Cielo Magno, extending parliamentary courtesy to the OP and OVP is “inappropriate.”

“The funds allocated to the OP and OVP are not entitlements. They are public funds. Like any other office, they should account and explain how they are utilizing the people’s money and what are the outcomes and impacts they achieved in utilizing public fund. They should also explain the purpose of the funds they are requesting,” she said.
Legislative oversight over budget should not exempt any agency, particularly the OP and OVP, according to Tim Salomon of the Caucus of Development Non-Government Organizations Network.
“There should be no sacred cows in legislative oversight of the budget,” he said.

articles.title: Gas, diesel prices to hit P100/liter
articles.summary: Hefty pump adjustments are set to push gasoline and diesel prices above P100 per liter at some fuel stations today.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Gasoline, diesel and kerosene prices will rise by as much as P4.69, P5.18 and P5.58 per liter, respectively, according to Energy Secretary Sharon Garin.
Rattanakun Thongbun via Canva Pro
MANILA, Philippines — Hefty pump adjustments are set to push gasoline and diesel prices above P100 per liter at some fuel stations today.
“We have an oil price hike, driven largely by higher international oil prices following renewed tensions affecting energy flows through the Middle East,” Garin said yesterday.
The weakening of the peso against the dollar also added pressure on domestic pump prices, with the local currency hitting record lows last week.
With the latest increases, gasoline prices in Metro Manila will reach as high as P102.04 per liter, while premium diesel will cost as much as P102.68 per liter.
Kerosene prices will range from P100.88 to P136.10 per liter.
Amid the ongoing energy emergency, the Department of Energy (DOE) is authorized to mandate the maximum price hikes and minimum rollbacks that oil firms can implement.
Rino Abad, director of the DOE’s Oil Industry Management Bureau, said domestic pump prices remain elevated as the geopolitical tensions continue to weigh on international supply chains.

Despite the absence of active peace talks, Abad still does not expect prices to immediately return to the peak levels seen during the height of the Middle East war, when prices climbed above P150 per liter.
While global supply flows have yet to normalize, the DOE reassured the public that the country’s fuel stockpiles continue to be sufficient and above the minimum required levels.
Fuel subsidy
Meanwhile, DOE officials said the government’s fuel subsidy program for public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers remains in effect this month, with funding averaging around P60 million per week.
Under the program, PUV and UV Express drivers will receive a P12-per-liter fuel discount, amounting to as much as P1,800 in weekly savings.

articles.title: DepEd addressing bullying in schools, Angara tells House
articles.summary: Education Secretary Sonny Angara on Monday assured lawmakers that the Department of Education (DepEd) is intensifying efforts to curb bullying and violence in schools amid growing concerns over…

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Education Secretary Sonny Angara on Monday assured lawmakers that the Department of Education (DepEd) is intensifying efforts to curb bullying and violence in schools amid growing concerns over student safety.

During the House committee on appropriations’ deliberation on DepEd’s proposed P975.96-billion budget for 2027, Akbayan party-list Rep. Percival Cendaña raised the issue of bullying and asked about the department’s measures to protect students.
“What is the DepEd’s plan to prevent bullying and violence within our schools?” Cendaña said.

“We have a lot of programs and we’re looking at the full implementation of the revised Anti-Bullying law. And we’ve seen functioning Child Protection Committees, which is a requirement of the Anti-Bullying law,” Angara answered.
More than 36,000 schools now have functioning Child Protection Committees, according to the secretary.
The department is also accelerating the hiring of school counselor associates under the Basic Education Mental Health and Well-Being Promotion Act.
The hiring process, which normally takes three to four months, has been reduced to 30 days.

Beyond school-based interventions, DepEd is also seeking support from parents and the wider community, with the education secretary noting that bullying can have complex causes rooted partly in the home.
“Because as we all know, the origins of bullying are quite complex and many have origins in the household,” Angara said.
Student stabbed, injured in school
Meanwhile, a Grade 8 student was injured after being stabbed by an older schoolmate during an altercation at the Buayan National High School in Barangay Buayan, General Santos City yesterday morning.
The 15-year-old victim was stabbed in the neck and abdomen and was immediately brought to a hospital by school teachers and barangay officials for treatment.

School officials said the 18-year-old Grade 11 student was subdued by security guards and teachers before being turned over to personnel of the General Santos City Police Office who responded to the incident.
Classmates told investigators that the two students had a misunderstanding, which led to the stabbing.

The General Santos City government dispatched social workers and psychologists to separately assist the injured Grade 8 student and help monitor the older student, who is now in the joint custody of school teachers and police.
Classes suspended
Meanwhile, classes in several areas remained suspended on Monday amid rains and flooding brought by the southwest monsoon.
In San Simon, Pampanga, classes at all levels in public and private schools were suspended from Sept. 7 to 11, except at Concepcion Integrated School.
In Santo Tomas, Pampanga, face-to-face classes at all levels in public and private schools were suspended from Sept. 7 to 12.
In Masantol, classes shifted to alternative learning mode until Sept. 8.
Classes at all levels in public and private schools in Calumpit, Bulacan were also suspended on Monday.
In Lingayen, Pangasinan, face-to-face classes in public and private schools were suspended on Monday.
In Batangas, in-person classes were suspended in Balayan, Calatagan, Lemery, Lian, Nasugbu and Tuy. – John Unson

articles.title: Remulla: VP Sara sought jail stay, handcuff photos
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp initially wanted her to be arrested and jailed at Camp Crame, asking about detention arrangements, including food, before deciding to proceed to the court to…

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte shows a document after posting bail at a court building in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp initially wanted her to be arrested and jailed at Camp Crame, asking about detention arrangements, including food, before deciding to proceed to the court to post bail, Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla bared yesterday.?

Remulla said Duterte’s team apparently wanted to generate images of the Vice President behind bars and in handcuffs. But the police opted to treat her with courtesy befitting the country’s second-highest elected official.?

“They wanted her to be jailed here. We said, ‘why jail her immediately?’ In the end, they refused, changed their minds and contacted us again to say they would go directly to the Quezon City court,” he said at a press briefing at Camp Crame.?
Remulla rejected claims that Duterte was harassed during the service of the arrest warrant, saying no SWAT team or armed police unit was deployed at her residence or office.
“It was coordinated very closely by the head of security and the CIDG. There was constant communication between parties. It was not a cloak-and-dagger thing,” he added.
“We made it clear that she will be accorded all the respect here. She will not be jailed and handcuffed, and she will be presented to court the next day,” Remulla said.
He challenged Duterte’s camp to release closed circuit television footage showing any alleged harassment during the service of the warrant.
NBI team
?Meanwhile, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has formed a team to validate Duterte’s claim that she is under surveillance, Director Melvin Matibag said.
Matibag said the NBI is willing to provide Duterte round-the-clock security and investigate any evidence she may submit regarding her claim.
VP security

Duterte’s security is continuously assessed by concerned agencies and necessary adjustments will be made based on validated information and prevailing threat, the Armed Forces of the Philippines said.
AFP spokesperson Col. Francel Margareth Padilla issued the statement amid claims by Duterte that there are threats to her life. – Helen Flores, Pia Lee-Brago, Rainier Allan Ronda, Ghio Ong

articles.title: DA: ASF fear caused pork price drop
articles.summary: Fears of another African swine fever outbreak, not over-importation, drove pork prices lower, the Department of Agriculture clarified yesterday.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am

Personnel from the Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Animal Industry and the local government of Quezon City inspect delivery trucks transporting livestock, poultry and meat products at an inspection site along Commonwealth Avenue in this file photo from August 2024.
Miguel Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Fears of another African swine fever (ASF) outbreak, not over-importation, drove pork prices lower, the Department of Agriculture clarified yesterday.
Price drops were a result of hog raisers selling their animals earlier than planned when the rainy season approached, increasing market supply, Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said.
“Rather than risk getting hit by ASF, or having an outbreak occur next door, they want to sell everything before they are affected,” Tiu Laurel said, describing the move as a “fastbreak.”
Last year’s ASF outbreak led to the increased prices of pork belly (from P450 to P490 per kilo) and shoulder (to around P400), he recalled.
Citing data from the Philippine Statistics Authority, Tiu Laurel said pork production in the second quarter climbed by 5.6 percent to 412,280 metric tons.
Average farmgate prices, however, fell by nearly 19 percent to P172.44 per kilo from P211.91 a year earlier.
In Mindanao, Tiu Laurel said hog prices declined despite little imported pork entering the region.

According to the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), the import volume for 2026 is expected to plunge by around 50,000 metric tons from 851,760 metric tons last year due to higher local production and import volume by food processors in 2025.
Tiu Laurel said once the BAI approves the commercial rollout of an ASF vaccine, hog raisers will expand production, which will stabilize domestic supply and reduce the need for imports.
“High prices encourage producers to expand, but disease fears can quickly trigger liquidation, creating sudden swings in supply and prices,” he said.

While the latest decline is a relief to consumers, Tiu Laurel said hog raisers are challenged to have greater protection from ASF for expansion, steady domestic pork supply and reduced reliance on imports.

articles.title: P14 billion in calamity funds released as of August – DBM
articles.summary: The government has released P14.02 billion in calamity funds as of end-August as it stepped up disaster response and repair efforts, with the bulk going to the Department of Social Welfare and…

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Motorists and commuters brave the knee-deep flood along Timog Avenue in Quezon City on Aug. 17, 2026 due to relentless rain brought by the southwest monsoon.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The government has released P14.02 billion in calamity funds as of end-August as it stepped up disaster response and repair efforts, with the bulk going to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) reported that the amount has been released from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) in the January to August period, leaving P26.13 billion still available.
The released fund accounted for nearly 35 percent of the NDRRMF’s P40.15-billion total appropriations for the year.

The total amount represents P23.49 billion for the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Program, P15.33 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program for local government units (LGUs) and P1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund, accompanied by P322.86 million in continuing appropriations.
The DBM said the DSWD was the biggest recipient, receiving P11.43 billion or about 82 percent of P14.02-billion total releases, mainly to replenish its Quick Response Fund (QRF).
QRFs are built-in budgetary allocations that represent pre-disaster or standby funds for agencies in order to immediately assist areas stricken by catastrophes and crises.
Once the QRF of any agency reaches 50 percent, it can request replenishment from the DBM.
The DBM noted that the DSWD received six QRF replenishment requests during the period, ranging from P1.72 billion to nearly P2 billion as of end-August.

The DSWD also secured P31.14 million for the repair and improvement of its Regional Disaster Response Command Center Office and Warehouse at Clark Freeport Zone, Phase I, as well as P13.64 million for two special purpose vehicles for disaster operations of its regional office in the Negros Island Region.

Meanwhile, the Department of Public Works and Highways received P1.85 billion in calamity funds while the Department of National Defense got P685.14 million and the Department of the Interior and Local Government received P50 million.

Under the proposed 2027 budget, the government has earmarked around P45.67 billion for the NDRRMF, or 14.7 percent higher than this year’s allocation, which is also seen to serve as a fiscal buffer for El Niño and other disasters.
Climate risk tool

Meanwhile, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources is promoting the use of the provincial climate risk diagnostic tool to map hazards and vulnerabilities in communities and to assist in planning local interventions.?
Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said the tool would help LGUs make decisions on climate adaptation and development through reliable evidence. – Andrew Ronquillo

articles.title: Defense: Names used for secret funds were aliases
articles.summary: The defense team maintained yesterday that the names used in acknowledging receipt of confidential funds for the Office of the Vice President and Department of Education were aliases.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense counsel Michael Poa (R) reviews documents during the 11th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial at the Senate on Aug. 3, 2026.
Senate SMU / Wendell Alinea

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team maintained yesterday that the names used in acknowledging receipt of confidential funds for the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd) were aliases.
Defense counsel Justin Nicol Gular made the statement in response to a question from Sen. Risa Hontiveros on whether the names appearing on the acknowledgement receipts were real names or aliases.

“Given that it has become a material matter, we have to couch this answer that it is classified information. But these are, in fact, aliases, for the consideration of this court,” Gular said during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia presented PSA Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande in connection with the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds allocated to the OVP and DepEd in 2022 and 2023, which department Duterte formerly headed.
Gular said the defense would address the matter at the appropriate time during its presentation of evidence.
“I will veer away from making conclusions of lower facts as of the moment,” he said.

The name “Mary Grace Piattos,” which is presumed to be fictitious, first surfaced during the House quad committee hearings last year and was believed to be among the informant-recipients of the confidential funds of the OVP and DepEd.
Gular said the defense only raised the issue of aliases and classified information in response to Hontiveros’ question.

“The only reason that was brought up, and to clarify, not only aliases but classified information, was because of the inquiry of our good senator-judge Risa Hontiveros. So, I don’t think it was timing. It was just a matter of what came up during the trial,” Gular said.
Grande earlier testified that the PSA has no record of the birth or death of any individual named Mary Grace Piattos.

articles.title: Leptospirosis breaches epidemic level in Manila
articles.summary: The number of leptospirosis cases in Manila has exceeded the epidemiologic threshold, the city health department announced yesterday.?

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Residents wade through floodwaters along Zapote Junction in Las Piñas on August 29, 2026.
Edd Gumban / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — The number of leptospirosis cases in Manila has exceeded the epidemiologic threshold, the city health department announced yesterday.?
According to city health officer Dr. Grace Padilla, a rapid increase over a short period was shown, with the number of cases rising from 1.27 percent last week to 3.48 percent.?
Manila logged 12 new cases yesterday, bringing the total number to 982. Up to 35 fatalities have been recorded.?
Padilla said district hospitals in the city have reached full capacity, including Ospital ng Maynila, Sta. Ana Hospital and Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital.?
At San Lazaro Hospital, medical center chief David Suplico said admission rates have declined although another surge is expected.?

“The leptospirosis situation brought about by the Aug. 17 flooding is starting to subside. What we are preparing for now is the flooding that occurred in Metro Manila on Aug. 29 and 30,” Suplico said.?
Mayor Isko Moreno said free doxycycline capsules are available across 44 health centers and seven district hospitals in Manila. ?
He also ordered the city health department and barangay officials to go directly to residents and distribute doxycycline to those affected by flooding in recent weeks.?
The Department of Health (DOH) reported that as of Aug. 29, Caloocan, Malabon, Navotas, Parañaque, Pasig, San Juan, Valenzuela and Quezon City have exceeded their epidemic thresholds.
Chikungunya
The DOH is also monitoring cases of the mosquito-borne disease chikungunya after recording a 38-percent increase this year compared to 2025.
Chikungunya, similar to dengue, is a viral infection that spreads through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes.
It usually causes sudden fever, severe joint pain, rashes, headache and muscle pain.?
From Jan. 4 to Aug. 15, a total of 887 chikungunya cases were reported, significantly higher than the 643 cases posted in 2025.?
However, the DOH noted a 57-percent decrease from July 19 to Aug. 1 with 77 cases reported, compared to the previous two weeks of July 5 to July 18 which had 181 cases.
The top three regions with high chikungunya cases are Eastern Visayas with 399, Ilocos Region with 259 and Calabarzon with 81.
Meanwhile, Davao Region and the Cordillera Administrative Region recorded 62 and 26 cases, respectively.
DOH data showed no death was recorded this year with one reported in the same period last year.
The World Health Organization said severe cases and deaths from chikungunya are very rare and usually occur in young babies or elderly people with comorbidities. – Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: Intel fund recipients match names of kids, dead people
articles.summary: A person who was recorded to have died 61 years ago and a two-month-old baby were among the supposed informants paid by Vice President Sara Duterte from her confidential funds.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 12:00am

Philippine Statistics Authority assistant national statistician Marizza Grande takes the witness stand during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte yesterday. Grande presented PSA records (inset) showing that many of the names listed as confidential fund recipients had no PSA records of birth, marriage or death. R
Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — A person who was recorded to have died 61 years ago and a two-month-old baby were among the supposed informants paid by Vice President Sara Duterte from her confidential funds.

This emerged yesterday at the resumption of the impeachment trial of Duterte, wherein Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) assistant national statistician Marizza Grande testified that the recipients of Duterte’s confidential funds included the names of 37 dead people and 25 minors. Grande called the discovery “unusual and unique,” during direct examination by private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia.
Grande said the PSA discovered that 1,685 of the purported recipients of Duterte’s confidential funds have “no records” at all in PSA’s database.

The PSA, Grande said, verified a total of 2,669 payees from the list of acknowledgment receipts (ARs) submitted as liquidation reports to the Commission on Audit by the Office of the Vice President and by the Department of Education which Duterte concurrently headed from July 2022 to July 2024.

The PSA official also revealed that a certain Beatrice Cuenca – born in January 2022 based on records – allegedly received P400,000 confidential funds, as shown on an AR she supposedly signed in March 2023.
Another individual, Mikay delos Reyes, was supposed to have signed an AR for P200,000 in 2023 even if her PSA records show she was born in 2020.
A certain Miko Alquizar was less than a year old, being born June 2022, when he reportedly received P400,000. Grande said there were 20 minors from the OVP payees’ list and five from DepEd’s.

Among the deceased “informants” verified by PSA were Fortunato Salig who died in 2011 but received funds in 2022; Emilio Togan who had been dead for seven years in March 2023 and Rodolfo Traya whose death certificate stated he died in May 2021.

Other alleged informants whose names the PSA found “unusual and unique” were Arthur Baon who received P50,000, Ralph Josh Bacon (P150,000), Beverly Claire Pampana (P130,000), Charles Sampaloc Jr. (P50,000).
The others were Xiaome Ocho (P100,000), Danrick Ocho (P500,000), Tomas Panda (P50,000), Tina Matching (P250,000), and Tinan Angelo Pusa (P100,000).
Responding to queries from Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, Grande testified there is “slim chance” that a living adult in the Philippines would have zero record of birth, marriage or death.
“There are people with no birth certificate who have record of marriage or death,” she said. “So maybe at least, one of those vital events will prove that a person exists.”

For his part, Sen. Bam Aquino urged the court to definitively establish whether the names on the controversial acknowledgment receipts were simply aliases, noting that pseudonyms would naturally not appear in the PSA database.
Not perfect

In his interjection yesterday – Day 22 of the impeachment trial – presiding officer Francis Escudero said PSA’s database appears to be not a “perfect” and “universal” record of the country’s population because of gaps in the registration system.
Escudero said this was the reason why Congress passed a law allowing the correction of clerical or typographical errors in a person’s birth records without the need for court order.
For her part, Sen. Risa Hontiveros recalled the PSA’s role in exposing the fake Filipino citizenship of convicted human trafficker and former mayor Alice Guo.

When asked by Hontiveros if the PSA believed that real people were behind the aliases listed as recipients of confidential funds, Grande said “we had no idea that these are aliases” when they performed verification upon the request of the House prosecution.- Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: Belugas transferred from Niagara Falls are under round-the-clock monitoring after deaths: Chicago aquarium
articles.summary: A Chicago aquarium says several of the belugas that were transferred to its site from Ontario's Marineland have health issues.

image.caption: A group of experts from Marineland and U.S. aquariums prepares to transport beluga whales onto a truck via a sling at Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont., on Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. (Carlos Osorio/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Hamilton·New
A Chicago aquarium says several of the belugas that were transferred to its site from Ontario's Marineland have health issues.
Shedd Aquarium says it is monitoring whales' hydration

Shedd Aquarium said in a Friday statement it is conducting round-the-clock supervision, and teams are monitoring the whales' hydration, breathing rates, swim patterns, social interaction and other behaviors.

The aquarium's update comes after it reported last week that two of the three whales that died at its site in a week's span were belugas from Marineland, a theme park in Niagara Falls, Ont., that closed after it ran out of money.
Shedd has said that Peekachu, one of the Marineland belugas, died on Aug. 25 at its site, two weeks after being relocated.
A 20-year-old beluga named Rain, which was moved from Marineland to the Chicago park in mid-August, also died, as well as a 34-year-old beluga that had lived for decades in Chicago.

items: Another beluga whale sent from Marineland to Chicago's Shedd Aquarium has died
'I tried to say goodbye and tried to tell him I love him': Canada's last captive whales leave Marineland

blocks.text: The Shedd Aquarium said there is still uncertainty surrounding the health of the remaining animals, and it is awaiting lab results as the park investigates the deaths.
"Some of the rescued belugas are showing more encouraging signs than others, but several have presented clinical concerns," Shedd wrote in the statement Friday.
"Their condition can change from day to day and, at times, hour to hour."
The aquarium said belugas get most of their hydration through the fish they eat, and while some of the rescued whales are eating regularly, others are not.
As a whole, Shedd said, none of the belugas are "where we want them to be from a health standpoint."
The Marineland belugas were given a clean bill of health in the days before their relocations, with Fisheries Minister Joanne Thompson responsible for giving the final approval.

Marineland, which is now up for sale, completed the largest collective move of captive whales the world has ever seen last week, shipping 30 belugas and four dolphins to five aquariums in the United States and Spain over several weeks.
Marineland threatened to euthanize belugas
The final move last week brought an end to whale captivity in Canada.
Before their transfers, Marineland threatened to euthanize them if it did not get an emergency cash infusion after the federal government blocked an earlier plan to move the whales to China.
The whales would have been euthanized if they couldn't be moved to new homes, said the park's adviser, Andrew Burns.
"We were out of money, out of time," he said, adding it's "unbelievable" that Marineland pulled off the complex operation.
Multiple whales have died after being relocated.
In 2021, Marineland moved five whales to Mystic Aquarium in Connecticut.

Two of those whales died within a year of the move, and a third died two years after the transfer. Mystic said the whales had pre-existing conditions while Marineland said they were healthy when they left.
Nineteen belugas, one killer whale and one dolphin died at Marineland between 2019 and 2025.

articles.title: Jonvic Remulla: Romualdez arrest pains me, but I'll do my job
articles.summary: Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday admitted that the arrest of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was difficult for him personally, as they are friends, but said he…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 11:36pm

Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday admitted that the arrest of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was difficult for him personally, as they are friends, but said he would continue to perform his duties without taking sides.
Remulla made the statement after authorities served an arrest warrant on Romualdez in connection with the ₱7.4-billion plunder case involving alleged anomalies in flood control projects.
“Mabigat man sa loob ko dahil kaibigan ko talaga 'yan, pero...ipinapakita lang namin na wala kaming pinapanigan," Remulla said after serving the warrant of arrest.
(It weighs heavily on me because he is really my friend, but... we are just showing that we are not taking sides.)
He also assured the public that authorities would carry out their mandate and ensure that Romualdez faces the judicial process.
"Huwag po kayong mag-alala, gagawin po namin ang lahat na madala siya sa hustiya," he added.
(Don't worry, we will do everything to bring him to justice.)

Police have secured Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering "a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack," according to Remulla.

Remulla went to the hospital early Monday night with PNP chief Police General Jose Melecio Nartatez to serve a warrant of arrest that the Sandiganbayan issued after the Ombudsman filed plunder charges against the Leyte congressman, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others.
A "24 Oras" report said Romualdez was read the warrant and his rights in the presence of his lawyer.
On Monday night, Romualdez sought the approval of the Sandiganbayan Third Division to grant him "continued hospital confinement" as he faces his plunder case.
A lawyer for Romualdez said he would face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess.

“We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” he added.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: No 10 condemns ‘thuggish’ far-right activists after Portsmouth unrest
articles.summary: Hundreds of men, some in balaclavas, try to prevent asylum seekers’ processing, two days after similar scenes in Dover

blocks.text: Downing Street has condemned the “thuggish and intimidating behaviour” of far-right activists who blocked roads in Portsmouth when a boat carrying asylum seekers arrived in the city, two days after similar scenes in Dover.
Hundreds of men, some dressed in black and wearing balaclavas, tried to stop the arrivals from being transported for processing until 3am, when police removed them with threats of arrest.

Hampshire police said later that a number of police, coastguard and Border Force vehicles had been damaged, and a few officers had suffered minor injuries. It said the force was investigating possible offences of assaults on officers and criminal damage.
The crowd was seemingly organised by Daniel Thomas, a far-right agitator closely linked to Tommy Robinson, the longtime anti-Islam and far-right figure whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon.

blocks.caption: Damage to a police car windscreen at the scene of the far-right protest in Portsmouth on Sunday night. Photograph: Supplied

blocks.text: Thomas was also behind the scenes in Dover on Saturday, when crowds of people dressed in black and wearing balaclavas blocked the road around the port.

Andy Burnham’s official spokesperson said: “The intimidating and thuggish behaviour we saw over the weekend in Dover and Portsmouth is absolutely unacceptable. We condemn it unreservedly. We’ll always respect the right to peaceful protest but not where it crosses the line into disorder.”

Thomas, who uses the name Danny Tommo on social media, was recorded telling the crowd that Portsmouth was “now ground zero” for the arrival of asylum seekers on boats from France, saying “enough is enough” and “Dover was a dummy run”.

Later on Monday he interrupted media interviews in Portsmouth with Zia Yusuf, the Reform UK home affairs spokesperson, to tell reporters that the use of balaclavas and masks was not intended to intimidate, but to stop supporters of his self-styled Patriot Platform group from being targeted by leftwing protesters.
Thomas was jailed in 2016 for the attempted kidnapping of a man connected to claims of drugs being sold, but now describes himself as a committed Christian.
The government had come under some pressure to condemn the events in Dover and Portsmouth as de facto vigilantism.

Nick Lowles, the chief executive of Hope Not Hate, which charts far-right activity, told the BBC: “To have 300, 400 people with balaclavas marching down the streets, stopping traffic. You know, it’s not just good enough. We need to call these people out for their politics and for the type of Britain that they want to see.
“We’ve got different ways to register our protest. We do not go on the street. We do not burn people out of their houses. We do not cause trouble and threaten to fight the police.”
after newsletter promotion

Reform UK’s leader, Nigel Farage, condemned the use of masks and paramilitary-style black outfits, but said the road blockades showed the UK was “on the edge of serious civil disturbance” over small boats carrying asylum seekers, even though the number arriving has fallen by more than 40% compared with the same period last year.

“Masked marches on the streets of Dover, and a huge, spontaneous protest on the streets of Portsmouth last night,” he said in a video posted on X. “You’d be right in thinking that this country is now on the edge of serious civil disturbance.

“But let me please say this: people wearing masks, dressed up in a similar type uniform to a paramilitary, is not going to solve this problem … Remember, peaceful protests good, uniforms and masks bad.”
Despite the fall in small boat arrivals, ministers will be alarmed by the apparent use of different routes by people smugglers, moving beyond the Dover area.

Donna Jones, the Conservative police and crime commissioner for Hampshire, said a boat carrying 140 people left somewhere near Cherbourg in France at about 1am on Sunday morning, before entering the Solent, near Portsmouth, about 10 hours later.

She said the town did not have the infrastructure in place to process arrivals, telling BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “My big concern now is that Portsmouth does not become a destination of choice for the people traffickers who are trying to bring people across to Britain.”
She did not condemn the far-right activists, saying: “Largely they were peaceful. They were there making their point, but they don’t want Portsmouth to become a destination.”

articles.title: Europe’s centre fears nationalist wave after far-right AfD wins state in Germany
articles.summary: ‘Historic’ win in Saxony-Anhalt may show voters’ discontent with political centre, but sweeping conclusions cannot yet be drawn

blocks.text: The numbers speak for themselves: Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), a party that dabbles in Nazi imagery, distinguishes between “biological” and “passport” Germans, and is too extreme even for France’s far-right leader Marine Le Pen, nearly doubled its score in Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt to 43.8% of the vote.

Meanwhile, the centre-right CDU of the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, collapsed to 17.2%, less than half its total in the same race five years ago, and the centre-left SPD – Germany’s other main party of government for the past 60-odd years – scraped 9.3%. The least that can be said is that the centre did not hold.

It is not yet clear whether the AfD, whose local branch in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt is officially classified by the country’s domestic intelligence service as “confirmed rightwing extremist”, will be able to form a government: it has 39 lawmakers in the 83-member parliament, just short of an outright majority.

But the score is the party’s strongest-ever state result and puts it closer to governing a German state than any far-right party since the second world war. It has sent shock waves round Europe, with nationalists cheering a “historic win” that is “just the beginning” and mainstream leaders warning of a “grave moment” for Europe.

Sweden holds legislative elections next weekend. France faces a crunch presidential ballot next spring. Key parliamentary races will follow there, as well as in Italy, Spain and Poland, later in the year. Far-right parties are polling strongly in all of them, and Europe’s centre fears a continent-wide nationalist wave.

It would be wise not to read too much into one election result in one quite particular German state. Saxony-Anhalt, analysts note, is home to barely 1.8 million voters and has long been a far-right stronghold: in federal and state elections over the past decade, support for the AfD there has consistently been double the national average.

“A far-right party winning a regional election in Germany is not more scary than a far-right party winning a regional election in France, the UK or the Netherlands,” said Tarik Abou-Chadi, a professor of European politics at Oxford University. “Saxony-Anhalt should not be the basis for sweeping conclusions about the electoral sociology of the AfD.”

Nonetheless, the AfD leads in national polls. It is also ahead – although in a far tighter race, with the SPD – in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where state elections are due later this month, and it is lying second even in liberal Berlin. Its rise is part of a decade-long march by far-right parties across Europe.

blocks.caption: The AfD is polling second even in liberal Berlin, and leading polls nationwide.  Photograph: Hannibal Hanschke/EPA

blocks.text: Almost one in four voters in Europe now cast their ballot for far-right parties, according to research led by Matthijs Rooduijn, a political scientist at the University of Amsterdam, a proportion that has grown nearly fivefold since the mid-1990s and climbed particularly steeply over the past three years.

This analysis, by more than 150 political scientists in 31 countries, found that the proportion of Europeans voting for a far-right party in their country’s most recent national elections had risen in 2026 to more than 23%, from about 10% a decade ago and roughly 5% in 1995.

Far-right populist parties are now in government as part of ruling coalitions in Croatia, Czechia, Italy and Finland, propping up a rightwing minority government in Sweden, and leading in the polls in Austria, Belgium, France and Germany (and, until very recently, the UK).

They have also suffered recent defeats, including in the Netherlands, where Geert Wilders’s Freedom party (PVV) lost nearly a third of its seats to finish second last year, and Hungary, where Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz was comprehensively beaten by his centre-right rival in April.
after newsletter promotion

But the trend seems clear. As Cas Mudde of the University of Georgia, a leading expert on Europe’s far right, put it after Orbán’s defeat: “The far right is here to stay, and many of its parties are as established as the (former) ‘mainstream’ parties. Like other parties, their electoral support fluctuates.”

That steady electoral advance has been achieved despite a refusal by mainstream parties in countries such as France and Germany to collaborate with far-right parties, prompting some commentators to argue that the “cordon sanitaire” or “firewall” has now failed, or even been counterproductive.

By keeping the AfD out, they argue, Germany’s mainstream parties have actually boosted it: the party has been protected from the compromises and failures inherent in government. At the same time, the centre has been “hollowed-out”: forced into uncomfortable, unstable alliances that agree on and – vitally – accomplish little, further frustrating voters and driving support for the extremes.

“There’s a self-reinforcing political dynamic that feeds the AfD’s rise,” said Mujtaba Rahman, of the Eurasia Group risk consultancy. “The weaker the election results, the less common ground in the coalition, the fewer the policy results. The fewer results, the bigger the frustration in the electorate, the bigger the AfD’s share of the vote.”

Many political scientists, however, say blaming the firewall is an excuse, and data suggests far-right parties do not in any case get weaker when they are in government, but become stronger: one recent study of more than 1,300 different governments in 57 countries found far-right parties that entered government averaged a score six percentage points higher come the next election.

Besides the persistent inability of mainstream governments to deliver for disillusioned voters hit by a spiralling cost of living crisis, it is above all the gradual mainstreaming and normalisation of the far right’s ideas that has driven – and continues to drive – its steady advance, political scientists argue.

Research suggests voter attitudes towards core far-right themes such as immigration have not changed significantly over time, but have become much more significant in their voting decisions: normalisation by the media and by mainstream parties that readily embrace far-right framing have legitimised far-right views.

“The entire debate about whether the cordon sanitaire is ‘successful’ or contributes to strengthening the far right completely misses the point,” said Gabriela Greilinger, an Austrian-Hungarian political scientist. “Far-right politics and policies already constantly take centre stage, whether or not the far right is in power. There is no cordon around their ideas.”

articles.title: Remulla to visit France amid Zaldy Co and Loren Legarda’s stay
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Monday said he will visit France to coordinate with authorities after Sen. Loren Legarda and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co stayed there amid…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Monday said he will visit France to coordinate with authorities after Sen. Loren Legarda and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co stayed there amid their cases here.
Legarda is facing a plunder complaint before the Ombudsman while Co is subject of two malversation cases now handled by the Sandiganbayan.
“I will go to France in the coming days to talk to French authorities, because France should not be a safe haven for plunderers and ill-gotten wealth,” Remulla said in a press conference in Filipino.
“Because Zaldy Co is there. Loren Legarda is there. So this is becoming a trend that, maybe, the country is being used as a hideout. We will make their world smaller,” he also said.

Co faces two counts of malversation over an alleged non-existent P77 million worth of flood control project in Bulacan and road dike project in Oriental Mindoro worth P289.4 million, which prosecutors said was found with structural deficiencies.

Legarda, along with her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, was accused by prosecutors of “conspiring to secure exclusive government rights over the country’s solar energy resources through legislative and regulatory actions,” resulting in more than P10.44 billion in unpaid financial obligations to the government.
Legarda, who first filed her medical leave on Aug. 3, extended her leave for the fifth time until Sept. 16.
Co, Legarda, and Leviste have repeatedly denied the allegations.
Remulla said he has no information if both Co and Legarda have already applied for asylum in France.

“I have no information, but that is (seeking asylum) now in the offing … but if they saw that they would have a reputation of being a hideout for ill-gotten wealth, I think the people there will also refuse them,” Remulla said. /cb

articles.title: PH optimistic for SCS Code of Conduct between ASEAN, China this year
articles.summary: The Philippine government is optimistic that negotiations for the South China Sea Code of Conduct between ASEAN and China will be finalized this year.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 11:28pm

The Philippine government is optimistic that negotiations for the South China Sea Code of Conduct between ASEAN and China will be finalized this year, as the Philippines is hosting its largest ASEAN-related event in November, the Leaders summit.

During the ASEAN Business Media Exchange 2026, Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim stated that every member of the regional bloc is “on board,” including ASEAN partner countries who are deeply involved in the long-awaited conclusion of the COC negotiations that have been ongoing between China and ASEAN for more than 20 years.

“This is unprecedented. It's never happened during the past few years. We're hopeful that this is one of the deliverables for this year: substantial completion of the negotiations on the Code of Conduct. And the entire ASEAN is on board,” he said.
Herrera-Lim added that "even China" is on board. “So we're guardedly optimistic that we will deliver on the promise on the Code of Conduct.”
The COC is an agreement that, when approved, is expected to establish clear rules in the South China Sea, including the West Philippine Sea.

However, years of negotiations have been stalled due to unresolved issues, including whether the COC should be “legally binding” and other key parameters that the Philippines considers important, such as the recognition of the 2016 Arbitral Award, which Beijing has repeatedly rejected.

With the aim of making significant progress in the negotiations on the Code of Conduct, Herrera-Lim said, one of the most significant developments for the ASEAN chairmanship is the Manila Plan of Action.

“The process for the ASEAN Chairship, the high note would be the Manila Plan of Action that will be approved this year under ARF, the ASEAN Maritime Center that will be established in the Philippines.”

The ARF Manila Plan of Action is a decade-long strategic framework established by the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) to steer regional political and security collaboration throughout the Indo-Pacific. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status
articles.summary: The long-running claim alleges Grindr breached UK privacy laws by sharing data with third parties.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
ByLiv McMahon
Technology reporter
Grindr has agreed to pay £26m to settle a lawsuit over allegations it shared users' personal information - including their HIV status - with third parties.
The world's largest LGBTQ+ dating app was sued in the High Court in 2024 over claims it misused people's personal information.
The class action suit was later served in the US, with the law firm leading the case saying it had signed up more than 11,000 claimants.
According to a US regulatory filing, Grindr will make two £13m payments to settle the claims. The firm said the settlement includes no admission of liability.
Grindr stressed the claims relate to "historical data practices" before 2020 when it was owned by Chinese firm Kunlun.
The filing submitted to the US Securities and Exchange Commission, external by Grindr said a settlement had been reached on 2 September.

"While Grindr disputes the allegations, it recognizes and acknowledges the distress and loss of trust expressed by some of its UK users regarding that pre-2020 period," the company said in its filing.
The firm has agreed to pay £13m to the counterparties by 31 December and a further £13m by 31 March 2027.
'Significant distress'
The claims brought more than two years ago by law firm Austen Hayes alleged Grindr had shared sensitive data with third parties for commercial purposes, breaching UK privacy laws.
It said this included information about the ethnicity and sexual orientation of its users.

People on Grindr have the option to share their HIV status along with when they were last tested - a move it says aims to reduce stigma, facilitate conversations and help users make informed health choices.
Chaya Hanoomanjee, the lawyer who led the claim, said in April 2024 claimants had "experienced significant distress" over their sensitive and private information being shared without their consent.
She said the company "owes it to the LGBTQ+ community it serves to compensate those whose data has been compromised".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Grindr became a publicly-listed company in 2022, two years after it was taken over by new owners

blocks.text: Grindr became a publicly-listed company in 2022, two years after it was taken over by new owners
Two data analytics services, Apptimize and Localytics, were identified as third parties with access to the sensitive data.
The claim said a potentially unlimited number of third parties used it to customise advertisements to Grindr's users.
It followed revelations in 2018 that Grindr had been sharing personal data, including the HIV status of its users, with the two data analytics providers.
Grindr defended the practice at the time as in line with industry standards – but it said it then stopped sharing HIV data with those companies.
It was fined £5.5m by Norway's data protection watchdog and, later in 2022, reprimanded by the UK Information Commissioner's Office for its data practices.
The company said in its filing on Friday that since 2020, it had "overhauled" its privacy practices to help meet the "unique needs of its community".
"Grindr is and remains a safe space for users, committed to transparency, user control, and responsible data practices," it said.

articles.title: Who is Martin Romualdez?
articles.summary: Born on November 14, 1963, Romualdez is the son of the late Leyte governor and diplomat Benjamin “Kokoy” Romualdez and Juliette Romualdez. He is also known as a “presidential cousin,” being one of…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 11:14pm
Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez has been placed under arrest on plunder charges, allegations that he has repeatedly denied and which his lawyer said he is ready to face in court.
Born on November 14, 1963, Romualdez is the son of the late Leyte governor and diplomat Benjamin “Kokoy” Romualdez and Juliette Romualdez.
He is also known as a “presidential cousin,” being one of the first cousins of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and Senator Imee Marcos.
His father is a brother of former first lady Imelda Marcos, the President’s mother.
Romualdez is married to Tingog Party-list Representative Yedda Marie Romualdez, with whom he has four children.
Romualdez has been the representative of Leyte's 1st congressional district from 2007 until 2016, and from 2019 to the present. His current term will run until 2028.
In July 2022, he was elected Speaker of the House of Representatives in the 19th Congress and was reelected for the 20th Congress with no other lawmaker nominated for the post.
He launched a nationwide campaign for the Senate during the 2016 national elections, ultimately missing a seat after finishing 15th in the final vote tally.

Before entering public service, Romualdez earned a Bachelor of Arts in Government from Cornell University in 1985. He went on to finish his law degree at the University of the Philippines College of Law in 1992 and passed the Philippine Bar Examinations in 1993.
Flood control scandal

On Monday, September 7, the Office of the Ombudsman officially lodged a P7.4-billion plunder case against Romualdez, former House appropriations committee head Zaldy Co (Ako Bicol party-list), Romualdez's personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Serenio, and Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation president Felicito Cristobal Guevarra.

The formal charge alleges that Romualdez and Co leveraged their official positions to routinely collect kickbacks, shares, and other financial gains totaling a minimum of P7.4 billion across at least 15 separate instances.
Later that same day, the Sandiganbayan Third Division issued warrants of arrest against them.

"The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the Third Division said.

"Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested," it added.
Romualdez has been placed under arrest at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City, where he is confined, citing cardiovascular health and a brain condition. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: French winemakers forecast 30-year low harvest after severe drought and heat
articles.summary:
Estimates suggest drop in production with vineyards also concerned ‘smoke taint’ from wildfires may affect quality

French vineyards hit by severe drought and heatwaves are expected to report…

blocks.text: French vineyards hit by severe drought and heatwaves are expected to report a 30-year low in wine production after the country’s hottest ever recorded summer, according to the agriculture ministry.
Initial estimates suggest winemakers will produce just under 34m hectolitres from this year’s harvest: a drop of 6% on last year, and 17% less than ‌the 2021-2025 average.

Agreste, the government’s farming food, forestry and fishing statistics body, said the drop was partly caused by a reduction in the number and size of vineyards, but mostly the result of extreme weather conditions.

“The summer was particularly hot and dry: soil drought has intensified throughout the country and heatwaves have caused localised sun scald, scorching, defoliation, and wilting of the grapes, reducing harvest volumes,” it reported.

blocks.caption: A grape picker gets to work at the Trois Terres vineyard in Octon, southern France earlier this month. Photograph: Guillaume Horcajuelo/EPA

blocks.text: However, some winemakers say with grape harvests still being conducted it is too early to make credible predictions.

The disappointing forecast comes after an optimistic start to the year, with heavy spring rains that encouraged grape growth. “The hot and dry summer conditions meant a deterioration of the [harvest] forecast,” Agreste reported.

A series of heatwaves brought the highest summer temperatures recorded in France since records began in 1900, with averages of 24C in June, July and August. Almost half of the country recorded temperatures on or above 40C.

Among the worst hit wine regions is Champagne where the grape harvest, which started unusually early in mid August, is predicted to be almost half that of last year. The Jura region in the east was the next worst hit with an estimated 37% loss. This year’s Burgundy-Beaujolais region grape production was expected to be one-third down, Agreste reported.

Winemakers in Bordeaux and the Languedoc-Roussillon as well as those in the south-east and south-west reported higher harvests this year but all except the Savoie region were down on the 2021-2025 five-year average for production.
However, Cécile Mathiaud of the Burgundy wine producers association said she was surprised by the government’s disastrous figures for her region’s vineyards.

“We know we won’t have a full harvest this year, but we have no definite figures and there’s no suggestion the situation is a disaster,” Mathiaud said. “We have some vineyards that have reported not much this year and others where it has been higher than expected.”

blocks.caption: The harvest under way early in the morning at Trois Terres. Photograph: Guillaume Horcajuelo/EPA

blocks.text: Some Burgundy vineyards began their harvest in early August but others are collecting the grapes now, she added. “Our reference is the historically low harvest of 2021 when we produced only 1m hectolitres; we think it will be higher this year, but the question is by how much? I have absolutely no idea how the ministry has come up with these figures.”
after newsletter promotion

Agreste said the figures were estimates and definitive results would not be known until regions made official harvest declarations later this year. It added that 2026 grape harvests were “marked by significant regional disparities”.

Wine harvests have traditionally taken place in France between September and mid October, but the climate emergency has brought dates forward slightly each year for the last four decades. This year, the harvest timetable advanced at least a week compared with last year throughout the country. Some vineyards in Bordeaux began two weeks early.

There are also concerns that vines and grapes in some of France’s best-known wine producing regions, including Bordeaux, have been damaged by smoke from rampant wildfires. No major Bordeaux vineyards suffered direct damage from the flames that came within 15km (9 miles) of the city, but there is concern that smoke has entered the grape skins causing “smoke taint” and affecting the taste of the finished wine.

The agriculture ministry would normally issue harvest estimates in early August, but postponed its analysis at the request of the wine industry because of what it described as “the high level of uncertainty surrounding these forecasts” caused by weather conditions and wildfires.
France’s wine sector is already under pressure owing to a decline in demand. Annual wine consumption in the 1960s in France was 127 litres each year compared with 40 litres a year now.
Wine drinking in the US, France’s largest export market, has also dropped and French wines have been hit by Donald Trump’s tariffs.

articles.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
articles.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected…

image.caption: Former Bosnian Serb army commander and convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic was buried in Belgrade on MondayImage: Oliver Bunic/AFP

blocks.text: Several thousand people lined the streets of Belgrade on Monday to follow the funeral service and burial of former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladic.

Earlier in the day, Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at the funeral service for the former general, who died while serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide in Srebrenica and other war crimes committed during the violent breakup of Yugoslavia in the 1990s.
In accordance with his wishes, Mladic was laid to rest at Topcider Cemetery beside his daughter, who died by suicide in 1994.

Informer TV, a staunchly pro-government broadcaster, carried live coverage of what it described as a "magnificent farewell," without mentioning the roughly 8,000 Bosniak civilians and prisoners massacred by Mladic's Bosnian Serb forces in Srebrenica in July 1995.
President Vucic not in attendance
President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend the funeral, citing a previously scheduled visit by his counterpart from Uzbekistan.
Observers say that the president has tried to chart a middle course on the issue of Mladic's funeral.

blocks.caption: Thousands gathered in the Serbian capital to witness Mladic's funeral procession Image: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Mladic was not buried with state honors, but with military honors, with Vucic insisting that the state was merely respecting the wishes of the family and ensuring a dignified burial.
"Were we supposed to forbid people from attending, forbid the funeral itself and create dog cemeteries?" he said in response to criticism from the EU.
The phrase "dog cemeteries" refers in Serbia to the unmarked graves of so-called "enemies of the people" who were executed by Yugoslav partisans during and immediately after World War II.

Vucic was equally dismissive of the decision by EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos to cancel a planned visit to Belgrade, calling her reaction "stupid." He has brushed aside other criticism of the public glorification of Mladic in much the same way.

An EU spokesman said in a statement that "Any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism contradict the most fundamental European values and have no place in the EU or in EU candidate countries."
Politically tricky time for Vucic
For Vucic, who has long sought to balance Serbia between the European Union and Russia, the situation is politically delicate.
He is expected to call a snap parliamentary election as early as this week. The poll is likely to take place on October 25.

blocks.caption: Mladic was buried with military honorsImage: Oliver Bunic/AFP

blocks.text: For the first time in years, there is a credible possibility that his ruling bloc could be defeated by the student movement, which has led anti-government protests in Serbia for nearly two years now.
Vucic is expected to head the list of his Serbian Progressive Party as its candidate for prime minister.
Elections also in Bosnia and Hercegovina
According to Dejan Bursac, a political scientist at the Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory in Belgrade, all signs point to a president increasingly anxious about the upcoming vote.

"Vucic is grasping at every available lifeline," Bursac told DW. "One of those lifelines is Mladic's funeral and the nationalism it can help generate, allowing Vucic to present himself as a patriot while portraying his political opponents as traitors."

Many Serbs, Bursac said, still feel deep resentment over the outcome of the Yugoslav wars and claim that crimes committed against Serbs during these wars largely went unpunished. "That sentiment is now being deliberately inflamed and politically exploited," said Bursac.

blocks.caption: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has brushed aside criticism from the European UnionImage: Djordje Kojadinovic/REUTERS

blocks.text: Tanja Topic, a political analyst from Banja Luka in the predominantly Serb entity of Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where Srebrenica is located, sees a similar dynamic.
"Politics here rests heavily on emotion," she told DW. "This is an issue around which citizens are mobilized. They forget how difficult their lives are because patriotic fervor takes over."
Bosnia and Herzegovina will go to the polls before Serbia, with elections there scheduled for October 4.
Students have a different focus

In Serbia, the student movement — a coalition of faculty assemblies and protest groups operating without formal leaders or public representatives — has largely avoided commenting on Mladic, the funeral or wartime crimes on its social media channels.

Analysts note that both Vucic's party and the student-backed electoral list, which is expected to include respected professors, activists and other public figures, are attempting to function as broad "catch-all" political platforms.
In Serbia, that means neither side can afford to alienate nationalistically minded voters. "Especially because the election will most likely be decided by a very narrow margin," said Dejan Bursac.
The students, he argued, have recognized that for many citizens, it is enough to campaign for the rule of law, democracy and against systemic corruption.

blocks.caption: The student movement, which has been leading anti-government protests in Serbia for almost two years, has largely avoided commenting on Mladic or arrangements for his funeral. Pictured here: people at a protest rally in JuneImage: Jelena Djukic Pejic/DW

blocks.text: The protest movement began with university blockades after the collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad, Serbia's second-largest city, in November 2024. Sixteen people were killed.
Although prosecutors have opened several investigations, including into possible corruption linked to construction contracts, no trial has yet begun.
The power of media control
Few people in Serbia place much faith in opinion polls. Nevertheless, it is widely assumed that both the ruling party and the student movement command roughly 40% support each.
The government directly or indirectly controls most television stations and major news outlets, many of which frequently publish identical content.
In recent days, pro-Vucic tabloid Informer has targeted anyone who describes Mladic as a war criminal, branding such critics as "professional haters of Serbs" and "traitors."

Yet political narratives in Serbia shift quickly. Vucic alone appeared on television roughly 400 times last year. By the time voters head to the polls in late October, he will almost certainly need a new issue to rally supporters around.
Mladic's funeral is unlikely to carry him all the way to election day.

articles.title: Stolen Generations survivors have more health challenges than other First Nations people
articles.summary:
Indigenous Australians forcibly removed under government policies more likely to have severe or profound disability, report finds

  • Get our

blocks.text: The tens of thousands of Indigenous Australians and their descendents who were forcibly removed under government assimilation policies have far greater physical and health challenges when compared to the wider Indigenous and non-Indigenous populations, according to a new report.

The report by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) was commissioned by peak advocacy body the Healing Foundation, which supports Stolen Generations survivors and their families, and builds on existing data released in 2023.

Released on Tuesday, the report reveals the stark inequities and the long-term inter-generational impacts of forced removals, a policy adopted by all Australian governments up to the 1970s under racist assimilation laws.

Children were put into institutions, or were fostered or adopted out to non-Indigenous families where many of them suffered harsh, degrading treatment and sexual abuse after being taken from their families. It is estimated at least one in 10 and possibly as many as one in three Indigenous children were removed from their families between 1910 and 1970.
The report uses survey data from 2022 and 2023 of Stolen Generation members, who are now all over the age of 50, and their descendants.
About 200,0000 people – or 45% of Indigenous Australians – have a parent, grandparent, aunt or uncle who was removed from their family, the report said.

Survivors were 2.7 times more likely to have severe or profound disability than other Indigenous Australians, and 1.7 times as likely to have been admitted to hospital in the past 12 months even when differences such as age, sex and remoteness of location were taken into account.

Compared to non-Indigenous Australians, survivors were six times more likely to have kidney disease, 4.8 times more likely to have a severe or profound disability, and 3.9 times more likely to report high psychological distress.

The report also found that Stolen Generations survivors experienced greater socio-economic challenges and distress, such as being less likely to be able to pay for unexpected emergency costs, or experiencing more days where they were unable to afford their essential needs.
after newsletter promotion
“In summary, the collective pattern indicates that Stolen Generations survivors experience generally more challenging socioeconomic circumstances than other Indigenous people,” the report said.

The report also found that Stolen Generations survivors were nearly twice as likely as other Indigenous peoples to report high levels of psychological distress, and 1.6 times likely to report experiencing mental or behavioural health conditions. Their descendants were 1.3 times more likely both to report high psychological distress and to be diagnosed with a mental health condition.
Dr Martin Edvardsson, the acting head of First Nations health at AIHW, said Australia lacked comprehensive data on the experiences and needs of Stolen Generation survivors and their families.

“Understanding the needs of Stolen Generations survivors through the existing data sources will be increasingly challenging as survivors grow older and become less well represented in household surveys,” Edvardsson said.

articles.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
articles.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

image.caption: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Saxony-Anhalt's Premier Sven Schulze spoke about the impact of the electionImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: There are situations in which politicians who have little left to say to each other still appear together before the press. This was certainly the case when Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) and his party colleague, Sven Schulze, the state premier of Saxony-Anhalt, discussed the results of Sunday's state election. They described the results as a catastrophe for the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) — an earthquake, a disaster. Merz appeared shaken and devastated, to put it mildly.

He thanked Schulze for his work during the campaign. Then Merz added: "Not only did something change in Saxony-Anhalt yesterday but throughout all of Germany. It will have repercussions, including on the international stage."

This is because the victors in the state election, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), oppose supporting Ukraine in the face of Russia's war of aggression, and many AfD politicians maintain close ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin's government, Merz explained.
No regard for the rule of law?
Speaking about the AfD, Merz adopted an almost confrontational tone. Majorities can change, he said, and democrats must always be aware of that and accept it.

But, Merz said, it is shocking that 60% of voters in Saxony-Anhalt chose parties that disregard the rule of law in Germany. Merz was talking about not only the AfD but also the socialist Left Party and the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), which split off from the Left Party over issues that align the BSW with the AfD.

In contrast, the chancellor said his government will always defend the values of the German constitution: "In our country, these values are not up for debate. Power is granted, not seized. And the minority is not the enemy of the majority."
Historians have long described the Nazis' rise to power in the German Reich as a "seizure of power," which is why Merz's statement is sure to be the subject of much discussion.

Seeking to reassure Germany's international partners in the EU and NATO, he said, "We know that Germany bears a special responsibility because of its history. We will always defend our political order and our firm anchoring in Europe."
What the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt win means for Germany
Could CDU politicians in Saxony-Anhalt help the AfD come to power?

Standing next to him, Schulze remained silent. On election night the previous evening, long after his defeat had become clear, Schulze repeatedly emphasized in numerous statements that the public's widespread dissatisfaction with the Merz government in Berlin had dealt him a massive blow.
As for now, the worst-case scenario has narrowly been averted: the AfD does not have an absolute majority in the Magdeburg state parliament — but only by the narrowest of margins.

And this is a problem for Friedrich Merz: Dissatisfaction is growing, even within his own ranks. Can he prevent individual CDU lawmakers in Saxony-Anhalt from voting — against the official party line — to elect Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD election winner, as head of government?
If not, then both of Merz's seats of power would be in serious jeopardy: his position as chairman of the party and his seat in the Chancellery.
Merz defends his controversial reforms

However, as of today, Merz is still defending the difficult reforms his government has undertaken. One such reform is the overhaul of the chronically deficit-ridden pension system, which will bring great hardship to many people in Germany and faced fierce opposition during the election campaign.

On election night, Vice Chancellor and center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) leader Lars Klingbeil suggested reassessing the reforms following the defeat of the coalition government in Berlin. However, Merz has not mentioned such a change in course.
How the AfD changed its pitch and broke through
AfD displays confidence

Hours before the chancellor's appearance at the CDU headquarters, the AfD took to the stage at the Federal Press Conference. The top candidate in Saxony-Anhalt, Ulrich Siegmund, sarcastically thanked the media, which had largely portrayed him during the campaign as a threat to democracy and the rule of law.
"It was also thanks to you that we made it," Siegmund said, adding, "Thank you very much for the great coverage during this election campaign."
For example, the influential news magazine Der Spiegel had recently labeled the AfD politician "Germany's most dangerous man" in a widely circulated cover story.

Siegmund then looked out triumphantly at the packed hall and declared, "Never before has there been such a wide gap between those members of the media who seek to dictate to us here in Saxony-Anhalt how we should live and the reality of life for the people in this state."

But Siegmund avoided the question about whether the election result is a clear mandate for his party to form a government — even one without a majority of its own, if necessary, or possibly with the tacit support of the economically left, populist Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW).

Siegmund, however, has said he does not want to be a partner in a coalition — he wants absolute power, and he doesn't have it. The situation in Saxony-Anhalt will surely be the subject of much discussion for many days, perhaps even weeks, to come.
This article has been translated from German.

articles.title: Matibag: Cayetano may face raps over 2019 SEA Games irregularities
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Alan Peter Cayetano may be included as a respondent in the charges that the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will recommend to the Department of Justice (DOJ) over…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Alan Peter Cayetano may be included as a respondent in the charges that the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will recommend to the Department of Justice (DOJ) over alleged irregularities in the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (Phisgoc)’s hosting of the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, according to NBI Director Melvin Matibag.
Matibag said this in an interview on Monday after announcing that the bureau is set to recommend filing cases against five members of the Phisgoc board of trustees, among others, in the coming days.

“He [Cayetano] introduced himself as the chairman. So it’s an ultra vires act. Pinakilala niyang chairman siya na parang nagpapatakbo. So posible na kasama siya,” Matibag said when asked if the senator would also be included in the case recommendation.
(He [Cayetano] introduced himself as the chairman. So it’s an ultra vires act. He introduced himself as the chairman as if he were running (Phisgoc). So it is possible that he will be included.)
The NBI director, meanwhile, did not specify what charges might be recommended against Cayetano and the Phisgoc officials.
According to Matibag, he met with two witnesses this Monday, noting that their testimonies regarding the supposed irregularities involving Phisgoc during the 2019 SEA Games strengthened the case.
He also said the bureau discovered that the P55-million SEA Games cauldron was contracted to different contractors.
“Siguradong may makakasuhan at siguradong may pagkakamali. Nakita na namin, very important ’yung kanina nakausap namin na witness,” said Matibag.
(Someone will definitely be charged, and definitely, there was an irregularity. We have seen it; the witness we spoke to earlier is very important.)
“Mas lalong dumami pa ’yung mga dokumento. I think we will need a few additional days this week para matapos namin,” he also said.
(The documents are piling up. I think we will need a few additional days this week to finish them.)
The Inquirer reached out to Cayetano about the matter but has yet to issue a statement as of press time.

Matibag earlier said that based on their initial findings, Phisgoc received around P6.7 billion in government funds, specifically from the Philippine Sports Commission, the Philippine Olympic Committee, and the Department of Budget and Management for the 2019 SEA Games.
He noted that if adding the other funds Phisgoc accepted from the private sector, the committee’s budget may reach over P10 billion. /cb
