articles.title: Northern Mindanao cops join global hunt vs cross-border syndicates
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — As criminal networks push past national borders, police in Northern Mindanao are locking arms with global law enforcement to track down fugitives and rescue human trafficking…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — As criminal networks push past national borders, police in Northern Mindanao are locking arms with global law enforcement to track down fugitives and rescue human trafficking victims.

The Police Regional Office-10 (PRO-10) on Monday marked the 2026 International Day of Police Cooperation, a global observance established by the United Nations. It is held every September 7 to honor the 1923 founding of the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) and strengthen cross-border security ties.
Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay, PRO-10 director, said local forces must work hand in hand with international agencies to keep modern criminals from finding safe havens in the provinces.

“We welcome the 2026 International Day of Police Cooperation and its theme, ‘Together Against Crime,’ as a timely reminder that unity, trust, and strong partnerships are essential in addressing threats that transcend borders,” Babagay told the Inquirer.
He said Northern Mindanao’s police force remains tightly coordinated with national and foreign counterparts to track down offenders and protect the vulnerable.

“The PRO-10, together with the Philippine National Police, remains committed to working with law enforcement agencies and stakeholders in sharing expertise, strengthening coordination, protecting vulnerable persons, locating missing individuals, tracking fugitives, and keeping our communities safe,” Babagay added. “Through cooperation and mutual respect, we can build a more secure and peaceful society.”

According to PRO-10, joint operations linked with Interpol initiatives have already helped authorities identify 17 child sexual exploiters, rescue 28 trafficking victims, and arrest 30 wanted foreigners./coa

articles.title: Iran plans to announce new ‘exclusion zone’ near Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: CAIRO — The new head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on Sunday said Tehran plans to announce an “exclusion zone” outside the Strait of Hormuz aimed at vessels it…

blocks.text: CAIRO — The new head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on Sunday said Tehran plans to announce an “exclusion zone” outside the Strait of Hormuz aimed at vessels it believes are attempting to transit the waterway.

Mohsen Rezaei’s comments to Iran’s state broadcaster came with few details, a day after the U.S. struck three Iranian oil tankers in response to Tehran launching ballistic missiles at U.S. warships. Experts called the launches a dangerous escalation after Iran’s previous attacks at sea targeted commercial shipping.

The new zone should be announced in the coming days and weeks and “will begin from the line of the U.S. naval blockade, extend toward the Strait of Hormuz, and from this side continue into the Persian Gulf,” Rezaei said. “Any ship that enters this area with the intention of passing through the Strait of Hormuz and is identified will be placed on our sanctions list.”

It is not clear where Iran defines the location of the weekslong U.S. blockade, which is aimed at Iranian ports and keeping Tehran from shipping out its oil. The U.S. military has said over 20 warships are supporting the blockade, which as of Sunday had redirected 92 commercial ships and disabled three.

The U.S. has been introducing new measures to increase the economic pain on Iran after negotiations collapsed and no end to the intermittent fighting appears in sight. Meanwhile, Iran continues to attack some ships trying to transit the strait, which has become an important source of leverage for Tehran in the war that began Feb. 28 with U.S. and Israeli strikes.
Iran earlier Sunday said it struck an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz, a claim that the U.S. military dismissed as a “total lie.”
Fighting resumed a week ago

The United States and Iran resumed attacks last week, following a month of relative calm, with the Strait of Hormuz and areas along Iran’s southern coast again being targeted. At least five people were killed earlier in the week during a U.S. bombardment that returned attention to the area where a school was hit in the war’s opening strikes.

The Trump administration appears to have adopted a dual-prong approach to the conflict, responding militarily to attacks on the strait while going after foreign financial institutions that handle Iran’s money.

But Tehran’s hard-line new senior leaders including Rezaei have signaled a willingness to dig in after weathering decades of sanctions. Iran has found ways over the years to circumvent sanctions, and now the U.S. blockade of its ports, and get its oil to buyers to help ease growing economic pressures.

“We had trusted our friends in Pakistan, Qatar or Oman, thinking that since they had stepped in as mediators, one of a mediator’s responsibilities is that if one side violates the agreement, they should stop them,” Rezaei said. “We are now pursuing diplomacy with guarantees.”
US says 9 million barrels of oil a day pass through the strait
The Strait of Hormuz is crucial to global oil and natural gas shipments and was seen as an international waterway before the war began.

On Sunday, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said that on average, 9 million barrels of oil a day are getting through the strait, which should help to relieve pressure on energy prices. His estimate appeared to exceed average flows over the past 28 days through the strait, according to TankerTrackers.com and other sources.
Wright told CNN that with oil also flowing through pipelines in the region, “we’re probably two-thirds or more of preconflict flows.”

But those flows depend on the presence of the U.S. Navy to help escort tankers and provide some protection against possible Iranian attack. Wright said he expected that other countries would eventually support the Navy’s efforts.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Rezaei in his interview with state TV claimed that “every day we are selling one million, one and a half million (barrels), as if Iran’s oil production and trade are continuing as usual.” /dl

articles.title: As climate change warms the Himalayas, disasters like the Nepal floods are becoming more frequent
articles.summary: KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — When a wall of water, rocks and mud tore through her remote village in Nepal, Pema Tamang and her neighbors fled uphill to a Buddhist shrine that had been rebuilt the previous…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — When a wall of water, rocks and mud tore through her remote village in Nepal, Pema Tamang and her neighbors fled uphill to a Buddhist shrine that had been rebuilt the previous year after a 2015 earthquake.
FILE -In this June 20, 2013, photo, the Kedarnath shrine, one of the holiest Hindu temples, and other buildings around it are seen damaged following monsoon rains in northern India. (AP Photo, File)

The steep mountain folds of the Himalayas, already prone to earthquakes, have seen more frequent flash floods as high mountain glaciers melt, redrawing rivers at sometimes terrifying speed. Residents have had little time to rebuild from one disaster to the next, raising concerns over whether their communities can endure as climate change accelerates.

“We were able to rebuild the stupa only last year after it was destroyed during the earthquake,” Tamang told The Associated Press, referring to the shrine. “Sheltering in it was how we saved our lives from the floods,” she said in a makeshift shelter at a monastery in Kathmandu.

The Aug. 26 floods in Nepal and neighboring China have killed more than 1,000 people and left thousands missing, including hundreds feared trapped in tunnels at hydropower projects. The floods were triggered after a collapse of bedrock and glacier ice sent debris and water surging through multiple Himalayan rivers.

Scientists say it is too early to directly link Wednesday’s catastrophe to global warming. But as Earth’s temperature rises at a faster rate because of the burning of oil, gas and coal, the chances of such disasters increase, especially in the Himalayan mountains, which are warming considerably faster than many other parts of the world.

“Climate change has been playing a large role in the Hindu Kush Himalayas, causing these kinds of complex disasters which have really impacted downstream communities and investments,” said Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk resilience expert at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development based in Kathmandu.
Global warming’s effects are heightened in the Himalayas
Sanyal said the region is increasingly confronting hazards that trigger one another.

Warmer temperatures cause high mountain ice to melt, leading to more frequent rockslides, avalanches and floods. An avalanche can dam a river before unleashing a flash flood. Heavy rain after an initial disaster can compound the destruction.

Flash floods last year in the same region in Nepal claimed nine lives and caused millions of dollars in damage. Across the wider Himalayan region, the 2013 Kedarnath floods, the 2021 Chamoli disaster, the 2023 South Lhonak glacial lake outburst flood, and other recent landslides and floods, have killed thousands of people and caused hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.

blocks.caption: A drone view shows rescue workers inspect the area and damaged structures following recent flash flooding along the Trishuli River in the Devighat area of Nuwakot district, Nepal, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

blocks.text: A drone view shows rescue workers inspect the area and damaged structures following recent flash flooding along the Trishuli River in the Devighat area of Nuwakot district, Nepal, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)
People in Nepal were still recovering from last year's floods, Sanyal said, “and before they could fully adapt, the next one came.”

The Hindu Kush Himalaya stretches across parts of Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and China, and contains the largest concentration of ice outside the polar regions. River systems originating in the mountains support nearly 2 billion people.

Glacier ice loss has accelerated sharply since 2000, according to Sanyal's intergovernmental climate research group. Another risk is thawing permafrost — ground that has remained frozen for long periods — that can weaken mountain slopes.

Satellite imagery of the glacial collapse last week indicates that a huge mass of bedrock and glacial ice plunged into a valley below, sending a wall of water and mud several stories high through communities many kilometers (miles) downstream.
Adaptation has limits in the mountains

Climate experts say that in some places the danger may become so great that rebuilding is no longer viable, forcing residents to move. Climate change could also have implications for efforts to develop the region through the construction of roads, bridges and hydropower plants.
“The adaptation threshold has been crossed in some areas,” said Manjeet Dhakal, a Nepali climate policy expert and United Nations climate negotiator.

blocks.caption: FILE -A man tries to recover a vehicle submerged in mud in a flood-affected area along the Teesta river in northeastern India, Oct. 8. 2023. (AP Photo/Anupam Nath, File)

blocks.text: FILE -A man tries to recover a vehicle submerged in mud in a flood-affected area along the Teesta river in northeastern India, Oct. 8. 2023. (AP Photo/Anupam Nath, File)

When an earthquake destroys a house, belongings can sometimes be recovered, he said. A catastrophic flood can wipe out not only the house, but the land beneath it, along with roads, water systems, schools and electricity. He said future resettlement would have to incorporate climate risk from the beginning.
The consequences can be mitigated by stricter land-use rules, better assessments before infrastructure is approved, stronger cross-border monitoring and early warning systems.

Still, Sanyal said that of the 670,000 people who received text alerts about the Aug. 26 floods, some were visitors or migrant workers who could not understand Nepali while others downplayed the risk. Other systems designed to measure rivers were overwhelmed or washed away.
Chanda Lal Chitrakar, a 62-year-old resident of Nuwakot in Nepal, told the AP that he paid little attention to warning messages. As the waters rose, he ran uphill to save himself.
Nepal suffers from the much larger emissions of wealthier countries

Sanyal said such warnings need to provide more information on what actions to take. He also suggested prioritizing development in less-dangerous areas, assessing infrastructure for multiple hazards and incorporating the knowledge of Indigenous communities into disaster planning.
Dhakal, the climate negotiator, noted that Nepal has emitted less than 0.1% of the greenhouse gases that cause global warming, even as it grapples with some of its most severe effects.

“We should blame those who are responsible for increasing the global temperature, those who have benefited from the fossil fuel economy for such a long time,” he said. “We can at least use this devastating example as an inspiration to urgently reduce carbon emissions.”

articles.title: Converge’s BizKarteng Pinoy podcast closes season 1 with clear message: PH MSMEs must embrace technology
articles.summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, or MSMEs, are critical to the Filipino way of life. In fact, they comprise the backbone of the Philippine economy as they make up about 99 percent of all…

blocks.text: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, or MSMEs, are critical to the Filipino way of life. In fact, they comprise the backbone of the Philippine economy as they make up about 99 percent of all businesses in the country while providing some 60–63 percent of the nation’s total employment and accounting for about 36 percent of the gross domestic product or GDP. Unfortunately, this critical sector is beset with challenges that make it difficult for business owners at this level to stay open, much less thrive. Filipino MSMEs face multiple interconnected challenges, with technology and digitalization representing a major and persistent barrier that limits their productivity, competitiveness, and growth. In this day and age, Filipino MSMEs are no longer just competing with the business next door; they're competing on a global stage—and they need innovation more than ever now. That reality anchors the Season 1 finale of BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast, the flagship business podcast launched in partnership with Converge SME Solutions. This final episode offers up a clear message: adopting the right technology isn't optional for entrepreneurs who want to scale beyond local markets. Instead, it’s a must. A Season Built on Real Stories Since its launch, BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast has focused on real-world Filipino entrepreneurship, featuring the growth journeys, setbacks, and eventual wins of local business owners and industry figures. Guests like Dawn Chang of DC Delights offered a firsthand look at how personal passions can be turned into scalable businesses. Others such as Char Tinio and Ned Adriano tackled the harder side of entrepreneurship, including recovering from failure, rebuilding, and managing the operational and financial pressures that come with running an MSME. Running through nearly every conversation was a common thread: technology adoption and reliable connectivity as tools that let local businesses compete and scale in a modern market—not as add-ons, but as infrastructure for growth. In other words, BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast touched on the real-world applications of technology, digitalization, and connectivity in running a business. Technology as the Path to Global Competitiveness That thread is what Season 1 ultimately argues: MSMEs that treat technology adoption as central to their operations—not peripheral—are the ones positioned to grow beyond the domestic market and hold their own globally. Whether it's the resilience required to survive a business failure, the operational discipline needed to manage finances, or the digital tools required to serve customers and scale, the season consistently points back to the same conclusion: competitiveness today is a function of how well a business leverages technology, not how big it already is. Taken together, Season 1 paints a fuller picture of what it takes to build, maintain, and ultimately scale a Filipino small business today: the personal journeys behind the brands, the resilience required to survive setbacks, and the digital foundation—connectivity, tools, technology adoption—that determines whether a business can scale past its starting point. Season 1 Goes Full Circle Rounding out the season's expert commentary is Dindo Marzan, Senior Vice President and Head of SME Business Group at Converge ICT Solutions Inc. Marzan is known across the industry as "Mr. MSME," and his insights on the broader MSME ecosystem and market challenges in the Philippines lend added weight to the season's closing conversation. Marzan's talking points get specific about what that foundation actually requires. Among them: why internet connectivity should be treated as a business investment rather than a household utility, and what separates residential internet from a connection built for business use. He also underscores why businesses need dedicated, reliable connectivity to keep daily operations running. Put simply this is the kind of connectivity that supports everything from customer service and digital transactions to cloud-based tools and long-term scaling. Just as important, Marzan flags some of the common misconceptions MSMEs fall into when choosing an internet solution, often underinvesting in infrastructure and then struggling to keep pace with demand. In other words, Season 1’s finale delves deep into the backbone of today’s digital era: strong, reliable connectivity. Ready to Level Up? Season 1 leaves Filipino entrepreneurs with a lot to chew on—real stories, hard-won lessons, and a clear reminder that going global starts with getting the fundamentals right at home. If you're building something and wondering what's next, this season's a good place to start.

articles.title: Meta pushes back on Philippine National ID integration for social media
articles.summary: Meta cites technical complexity for integrating the Philippine National ID for user verification. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has urged Meta to integrate the…

blocks.text: Meta cites technical complexity for integrating the Philippine National ID for user verification. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has urged Meta to integrate the national ID as part of their process for Filipinos to gain access to Meta platforms, which are: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and Threads. The meeting happened in Singapore. There, DICT Secretary Henry Aguda told Meta about the integration of the Philippine national ID. He cited Roblox was able to promise to do so. Part of the reason to the urge to integrate the national ID is to curb online crime, fraud, and child-safety risks. Meta pointing out technical complexity should not be considered a refusal. But it is a show of reluctance. At the very least, Meta has pushed back on the immediacy and the scope of the integration of the national ID. Meta has, however, committed to send a technical working group to the country to collaborate with National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), and the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on identity-verification features. The CICC claimed Meta will not receive direct ass to the national ID database. Instead, Meta will be able to send identification or reference number to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), which would only show a "match" or "no match." Personal data would remain with the government.

articles.title: Kakie Pangilinan on KC Concepcion: ‘Every family naman has conflict’
articles.summary: Kakie Pangilinan acknowledged that there is a strain in her relationship with half-sister KC Concepcion. But she made one thing clear: she still loves her. “Every family naman has conflict, you know,…

blocks.text: Kakie Pangilinan acknowledged that there is a strain in her relationship with half-sister KC Concepcion. But she made one thing clear: she still loves her. “Every family naman has conflict, you know, and we’re working on it,” Kakie said in an interview with Ogie Diaz. Kakie was asked about KC amid observations that they have not been in communication for quite some time. She did not go into the details of what happened, choosing to keep some matters within the family. But she was candid about how she sees KC. “I love her very much. I love my sister very much and I think I can say I miss my sister very much,” Kakie said. She also pushed back against the idea that she treats KC differently because they are only half-sisters. “Never ko pong naisip na half-sister ko siya,” she said, adding that while they are biologically half-sisters, she has always considered KC her sister. Kakie also shared that even with the distance between them, KC remains part of the family in her mind. She recalled how she would include KC’s name whenever she ordered birthday cakes for her parents. The distance, however, is real. Kakie admitted that they have not seen or spoken to each other for a long time. She also made a distinction between having disagreements and having a full-blown family fight. “Hindi naman porket disagreements automatic na fight or away na agad,” she said. Kakie said there are also plenty of things being said about their family online that do not necessarily reflect what actually happened. It remains to be seen whether KC will respond to Kakie’s first extended public remarks about their relationship.

articles.title: Typhoon Saudel: Mudslide death toll in China rises to 3
articles.summary: BEIJING — The death toll from a mudslide in eastern China rose to three on Sunday, after days of torrential rain brought by Typhoon Saudel. Nine others were still missing. The mudslide hit part of a…

blocks.text: BEIJING — The death toll from a mudslide in eastern China rose to three on Sunday, after days of torrential rain brought by Typhoon Saudel. Nine others were still missing.

The mudslide hit part of a village in Suichuan County in Jiangxi province early Saturday, damaging a dozen houses. Rescuers found two people dead on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported. More than 5,300 people in the county were relocated to safer places. A third death related to the typhoon was reported Saturday.

Separately, CCTV reported that two people were killed in Hunan province in south-central China following downpours brought by the typhoon. The report didn’t specify the cause of the deaths, but said that the rain triggered landslides and other disasters.

Saudel made two landfalls in Zhejiang Province on Aug. 28 and made a third landfall as a tropical storm in Fujian Province on Sept. 3, Chinese official news agency Xinhua reported. Both provinces neighbor Jiangxi.
Xinhua also reported Sunday that a person was killed after a landslide struck another village in Jiangxi a day before, but it didn’t specify whether Saudel triggered it. /dl

articles.title: New Delhi building collapse: Three killed, others trapped
articles.summary: NEW DELHI — A building collapse in the Indian capital New Delhi killed at least three people on Sunday, local media reports said, as authorities worked to rescue those trapped in the rubble.…

blocks.text: NEW DELHI — A building collapse in the Indian capital New Delhi killed at least three people on Sunday, local media reports said, as authorities worked to rescue those trapped in the rubble.

The building, housing mostly students, came crashing down about midday in the southwestern Satya Niketan area of the city, with police and disaster response personnel cautiously lifting the rubble using heavy machinery.
Three people died in the accident, according to The Hindu newspaper and other local media reports, quoting unnamed fire services officials.
Nine people were rescued from under the rubble, with five of them taken to a hospital in critical condition, the reports said.
The exact number of people feared trapped was not immediately known.
An adjacent building has been vacated over fears it could also collapse.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the incident was “distressing” and offered “condolences to those who lost their loved ones”, according to a statement from his office.
TV images showed rescuers pulling a young man out from the rubble and another trapped under a block of fallen concrete slab, with only his face visible.
Delhi’s Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said she was “deeply concerned” by the incident.
“Every possible effort is being made to safely rescue those trapped and provide immediate assistance to the affected families,” Gupta said in a social media post.
The Satya Niketan area is home to hundreds of university students living in crowded, privately-owned accommodations as paying guests.
Building collapses are frequent in India, and illegal structures — often home to migrant workers and students — are common in big cities.
Last year, at least 11 people were killed after a residential building collapsed in the northeastern district of the capital city. /dl

articles.title: Filipinos bag 6 medals at Toyota Asia Pacific Skills Contest
articles.summary: Toyota Motor Philippines Corporation (TMP) brought home a landmark win for the Philippines after its Filipino delegation earned six medals across all categories in the Toyota 2026 Asia Pacific Skills…

blocks.text: Toyota Motor Philippines Corporation (TMP) brought home a landmark win for the Philippines after its Filipino delegation earned six medals across all categories in the Toyota 2026 Asia Pacific Skills Contest (ASPAC), emerging as one of the competition's strongest performers among 11 Toyota affiliates across the region. Held at the Toyota Motor Thailand’s Ban Pho Plant in Chachoengsao Province, this historic achievement marked TMP’s first complete podium sweep in all categories, as well as breakthrough medals in two contest categories, since first joining the annual competition in 2006. Filipino talent among Asia’s best The ASPAC is a highly competitive regional skills competition organized by Toyota Motor Asia for Line Team Members and Leaders from Toyota affiliates from Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Pakistan, and India to demonstrate their technical mastery in shopfloor skills anchored on the Toyota Production System. Christian Cobilla and Wilmer Penalla, who respectively competed in the ‘Painting - Team Leader’ and ‘Logistics - Team Member’ categories, earned silver medals. Noel Elpos, Edwin Bocaya, Loreto Muyna, and Ramel Sarmiento, clinched bronze for their performance in the Logistics, Assembly, Quality Control, and Welding categories. Since 2006, TMP has brought home 14 medals for the Philippines, including its fourth gold last year. The combined feat of these highly skilled TMP Team Members cements the Philippines not just as the fourth-largest market of global Toyota in Asia, but also as a hub of top-notch manufacturing talent in the region. Vehicle for Philippine development This momentous win extends the celebration of TMP’s recently marked 38th anniversary—a testament to decades of nation-building by nurturing local production capabilities and world-class talent of Filipinos in automotive manufacturing. Historically, TMP has recorded over 1.2 million units produced locally. This is made possible through the flexibility and precision of its highly skilled Filipino workforce, which can now produce over 60,000 units per year of Completely-Knocked-Down (CKD) models—the Vios, Innova, and Next Generation Tamaraw—at TMP’s Santa Rosa plant. Following the start of operations of TMP’s in-house vehicle conversion facility, the company gained a new capability of converting the Next Generation Tamaraw into six body configurations. This new investment continues to shape a robust industry where Filipino vehicle designers, engineers, parts suppliers, and body builders can upskill and manufacture vehicles essential to local development such as utility vans, ambulances, and more.

articles.title: AUDIOJUNKIE: The Ella Langley effect
articles.summary: By now you’ve probably heard the song “Choosin’ Texas” by Ella Langley on the radio. I don’t know about FM radio in Manila, but in the US, Langley is ridin’ high. I mean, I always hear “Choosin’…

blocks.text: By now you’ve probably heard the song “Choosin’ Texas” by Ella Langley on the radio. I don’t know about FM radio in Manila, but in the US, Langley is ridin’ high. I mean, I always hear “Choosin’ Texas” every time I open my radio. More often while driving, in the morning, which I never miss, and once more in the evening on my way home. There’s something to be said about that. For one to play on radio so dominantly (even in this day and age) you’ve got to be a big time artist. And these days, no one is as big as Langley. By now, “Choosin’ Texas” has already spent 45 weeks in the Hot 100 Billboard Charts. I don’t know how long it stayed on number one, but as I’m writing this, it’s still enjoying the top spot as we speak. Now that’s something! Ok, I researched it: “Choosin’ Texas” has spent 20 weeks (!) on the singles charts. Not only that, in its course, it has broken and made several records among which, it is the longest female song on the chart, beating out Mariah Carey and BoyZ II Men’s “One Sweet Day.” It is also the longest leading non-holiday song in the charts’ history. And it is the longest running No. 1 country song by a female artist in the 68-year history of the singles charts. Not bad. But who is Langley, really? Well, she was born May 3, 1999 and she is from Hope Hull, Alabama. This home grown country girl stands about 5’6”. She made her debut as a country artist back in 2024 with a duet (with Riley Green) titled “You Look Like You Love Me.” This song is a ditty, simplistic enough to listen to and sing, and the melody is not that hard to retain, but far from being a hit. But that’s the great thing about artists, you don’t know which of their songs can be a hit. “Choosin’ Texas” is different. After a four-bar intro that can be likened to any classic 80’s country song, the song comes in easy: “Just when I thought I got him to fall in love with Tennessee / I shoulda known better than to take him back to Abilene / I put him right back into her arms / I wasn’t a match for that kinda spark.” I mean, what’s in Abilene? And who is that other woman? From there, you just gotta see where it takes you. You don’t need to be a country music fan (I mean look at me) to be reeled into the mystery. And it’s even plain speak: “She’s from Texas, I can tell by the way / He’s two steppin’ ‘round the room.” Why the hell is he doin’ that? “And judgin’ by the smile that’s written on his face / there’s nothin’ I can do...” Just about seems to seal this sorry girl’s fate! Even the song references are on point! “Smoky Mountain Rain” is a Ronnie Milsap tune, and “them old Hank tunes, the Memphis blues we used to sing” refer to Hank Williams! And “he always loved ‘Amarillo By Morning’” is a George Strait song. That’s an old country gangster roll call right there. But other than that, this brown-haired girl really sings a pretty tune. She’s this season’s Shania Twain; this summer’s Linda Ronstadt; and she’s just about to enter the Dolly Parton era of her career. That’s the Ella-Langley-effect there!

articles.title: Tropical Storm Krovahn may not re-enter PAR but continues to enhance ‘habagat’
articles.summary: The tropical storm with the international name “Krovahn” now has only a slim chance of re-entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), but it will continue to enhance the southwest monsoon…

blocks.text: The tropical storm with the international name “Krovahn” now has only a slim chance of re-entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), but it will continue to enhance the southwest monsoon or “habagat” and bring more rain over parts of Luzon, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Monday, Sept. 7. PAGASA weather specialist Aldczar Aurelio said Krovahn, formerly called “Pilandok,” was located 1,155 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon as of 3 a.m. Monday, moving eastward at 10 kilometers per hour. Krovahn exited the PAR on Sept. 3. Over the next 24 hours, occasional heavy rains may persist over Zambales, Bataan, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro due to the enhanced habagat. Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Antique, and the rest of Central Luzon, Calabarzon, and Mimaropa may experience cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms. The rest of the country may have partly cloudy skies with chances of isolated rain showers or thunderstorms. Meanwhile, Ambuklao and Binga dams in Benguet and San Roque Dam in Pangasinan continued to spill excess water, based on PAGASA’s monitoring. As of 8 a.m. Monday, two gates of Ambuklao Dam were open. Its water level was at 751.41 meters, just 0.59 meter below its 752-meter normal high water level. Binga Dam’s water level was at 573.9 meters, or 1.1 meters below its 575-meter normal high water level. Two of its gates remained open. San Roque Dam was at 279.46 meters, just 0.54 meter below its normal high water level, although this was lower than the 282.08 meters recorded the previous day. Two of its gates also remained open. The three dams form part of a cascading system, with water released from Ambuklao mostly flowing into Binga Dam before Binga’s releases move downstream to San Roque Dam.

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ makes it 6 weeks in a row at No. 1 as Hollywood wraps a banner summer
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” remained the No. 1 movie in theaters over the weekend, becoming just the second film this decade to top the box office for six straight weeks. Since the…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” remained the No. 1 movie in theaters over the weekend, becoming just the second film this decade to top the box office for six straight weeks. Since the end of July, the Sony superhero movie has ruled over cinemas with rare dominance. The last release to enjoy such a long stretch leading the box office was 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water.” “Brand New Day,” the fourth standalone Spider-Man film starring Tom Holland, collected $18 million over the weekend, according to studio estimates Sunday. Sony is forecasting $23.3 million for the four-day holiday weekend. “Brand New Day” has grossed $2.4 billion worldwide. Universal Pictures’ “The Odyssey,” as it has for much of the “Spider-Man” run, remained in second place. Christopher Nolan’s epic added $13 million domestically over the weekend, bringing its global haul to $1.63 billion. More than $1 billion of that has come from overseas sales, making “The Odyssey” the first to achieve that international milestone since 2009’s “Avatar.” Both blockbusters — “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” — helped lead Hollywood to its best summer since before the pandemic. Through Aug. 31, the domestic box office totaled $4.6 billion for the season, according to Rentrak, an increase of 26.1% from 2025 and just shy of 2013’s record summer. On Sunday, Rentrak forecast that, including the Labor Day weekend, the summer will end up with $4.759 billion, a whisker above the $4.758 billion of summer 2013. That time frame, though, spans 130 days this year, compared with 123 days in 2013. Accounting for inflation and higher ticket prices, Hollywood’s summer wasn’t quite so historically sensational. Admissions are still well below pre-pandemic marks. But it’s nevertheless a remarkable rebound for a film industry that has struggled to string together such a hit-filled summer through the pandemic, labor strife and the expansion of streaming. Labor Day weekend is typically a sleepy time in theaters. And neither new release — Paramount’s “By Any Means” and A24’s “Onslaught” — made much of a mark. One of the weekend’s best performers was “Coyote vs. Acme,” the hybrid live-action-animated Looney Tunes movie. It dipped a modest 29% to gross $11.3 million in its second weekend. “Coyote vs. Acme” is turning out to be a good investment for Ketchup Entertainment. The indie distributor acquired the film for approximately $50 million after Warner Bros., which produced the $70 million film, opted to can it. In two weeks, “Coyote vs. Acme” has ridden strong reviews and good word-of-mouth to $33.8 million domestically. “By Any Means,” a 1960s-set civil rights action thriller starring Mark Wahlberg and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, opened with $7.4 million. Paramount is projecting $9.2 million for the four-day holiday weekend. Audiences gave it a “B+” CinemaScore. “Onslaught,” however, flopped with $1.9 million on 1,918 screens for the three-day weekend and a projection of $2.3 million for the four-day weekend. The A24 release, directed by Adam Wingard, stars Adria Arjona as a former Army sniper who defends her trailer park home from three escaped, experimental super soldiers. “Onslaught” cost a modest $15 million to make. But reviews (57% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) and audience scores (a “C” CinemaScore) weren’t good. Meanwhile, “Buddy,” a low-budget dark comedy, has turned into a surprise success. Made for just $3 million, the film, directed by Casper Kelly and from the producers of “Weapons,” is about a group of children trapped inside a surreal 1990s children’s television series. After overperforming in its opening weekend, “Buddy” actually increased its ticket sales over its second weekend. The film grossed $5.7 million, up 5%, to bring its two-week total to $14.3 million. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $18 million. 2. “The Odyssey,” $13 million. 3. “Coyote vs. Acme,” $11.3 million. 4. “By Any Means,” $7.4 million. 5. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $6.5 million. 6. “Cars” (20th anniversary): $6.1 million. 7. “Buddy,” $5.7 million. 8. “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie,” $3.3 million. 9. “The End of Oak Street,” $2.9 million. 10. “The Dog Stars,” $2.7 million.

articles.title: 'Lego Mandalorian': Cute, silly, fun
articles.summary: Announced earlier at D23, Mano and Grogu get the Lego treatment in a new one shot special on Disney Plus. Star Wars and Lego are old friends having collaborated on some of the best (and most…

blocks.text: Announced earlier at D23, Mano and Grogu get the Lego treatment in a new one shot special on Disney Plus. Star Wars and Lego are old friends having collaborated on some of the best (and most expensive!) Lego sets in recent years. If you’re a fan of the Lego film, then you’ll sink into this one pretty easily. The premise is that Manodo and Grogu get suckered into a surprise birthday party for Mando under the pretense of a new and dangerous bounty. Once there they get the best kind of ambush, one with friends, party hats and lots of blue milk. The short is a summary of sorts, a retelling of the three seasons of the acclaimed Mandalorian show, told in the unique Lego style. Being a recap, I’d have thought that this would be released before the Mandalorian and Grogu movie to catch people up on the story thus far but unfortunately it did not. Still, it is a blast seeing the story of Mando and Grogu retold in the off-beat, self aware style that the Lego movies are known for. It is jam-packed with visual gags that make full use of the fact that the characters and sets are lego building blocks. And the wit is there as well, as the characters take turns exaggerating events from the past, lampooning what happened or spinning tall tales, hilariously embellishing what actually took place. If anything the short suffers from being too short. There is so much material to draw from and make fun of over the three seasons of the Mandalorian that often the show seemed overly-stuffed. Taking the extra fifteen minutes to make it a full hour could have spaced the jokes out a bit more, but that’s a small little nitpick. ''Lego Mandalorian'' is a cute, silly way to look back on what was definitely a highlight of the Disney Plus Star Wars crop of shows. It does feel a bit like a farewell, especially knowing that a new season is nowhere on the horizon. It its good to know in whatever form, Mando and Grogu are fixtures now in Star Wars lore, and one way or another, they’ll keep coming back.

articles.title: Amazon cargo plane overshoots Miami runway: 5 dead, 5 injured
articles.summary: MIAMI, United States — At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, crashed into vehicles and caught…

blocks.text: MIAMI, United States — At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, crashed into vehicles and caught fire, officials said.

Miami-Dade County fire chief Ray Jadallah told reporters that in addition to five fatalities, three people were transported to trauma centers “in critical condition” and two more were treated at a local hospital.
“The airplane did strike a couple of vehicles,” which left “a couple of victims that were actually trapped in the vehicles,” Jadallah said.
“A complex extrication with our technical rescue team” was needed, “including a search and rescue of the pilot and co-pilot that were trapped in this aircraft.”
Jadallah did not clarify whether the pilot or co-pilot survived, and officials declined to answer questions after brief statements were made.
Video showed thick smoke billowing from the blue and white Boeing 767 that had arrived around 2 pm (1800 GMT) from Puerto Rico, as fire trucks raced to the scene.
The plane operating as Prime Air Flight 7598 caught fire as a result of the “crash,” fire officials said.
“A total of 60 fire apparatuses arrived, just short, just shy of 200 men and women from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, to begin the actual search and rescue and firefighting,” Jadallah said.
“The actual cause of the incident will be determined by the FAA and the NTSB,” he added, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board.

The NTSB said in an X post on Sunday the B-767-300 cargo airplane was flying into Miami from San Juan, Puerto Rico and they have “launched a go team to investigate Sunday’s runway excursion accident.”

The airport closed all runways and taxiways because of the incident and posted an update to its website Sunday evening that travelers should check directly with their airline before heading to the airport.
Amazon put out a statement saying the aircraft “experienced an incident while attempting to land.” It did not say if anyone was hurt or killed.

“This is a fast-moving situation and we’re still gathering details. We’re working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in the statement.
Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz told reporters Sunday that her officers encountered a “really tragic scene,” but there was “no apparent threat to public safety.” /dl

articles.title: ICC chief Akane vows to continue job no matter what amid US sanctions
articles.summary: Tomoko Akane, president of the International Criminal Court, vowed on Sunday that she will continue to do her job, despite the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump imposing sanctions on her…

blocks.text: Tomoko Akane, president of the International Criminal Court, vowed on Sunday that she will continue to do her job, despite the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump imposing sanctions on her and other officials of the Hague-based judicial body.

“No matter what happens, my convictions will not waver. I will continue to conduct investigations, prosecutions and judicial proceedings as I have until now,” she said, appearing online at an event in Tokyo.
She is among the ICC judges targeted by U.S. sanctions that freeze assets in the United States, with Washington accusing the ICC of encroaching on state sovereignty.
Akane, the first Japanese national to head the ICC, described the punitive measures as a threat to judges and to the principle of neutrality.
Speaking about the threat to the rule of law from the sanctions, Akane said, “Silence is tantamount to accepting rule by overwhelming pressure or force,” adding, “I will not give up.”
The Trump administration has strongly objected to ICC probes into alleged war crimes committed by U.S. military personnel.
Akane also urged Japan to take a proactive role in efforts to cooperate with many countries and prosecute serious crimes, calling on it to “actively join the global effort now.”

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has said the sanctions were “incompatible” with her country’s commitment to the rule of law, after initially coming under scrutiny over her initial remarks that the measures were “very unfortunate,” in language seen as stopping short of criticizing Japan’s sole treaty ally.
On Friday, Gen Nakatani, a former defense minister who leads a nonpartisan parliamentary group advocating human rights diplomacy, called on Takaichi to urge Washington to retract the sanctions.
“Upholding the Japan-U.S. alliance and defending the rule of law is not a choice between two options,” he said.
A former prosecutor, Akane became president of the ICC in March 2024. Japan is the largest financial contributor to the court. /dl

articles.title: 1 dead, 6 hurt as SUV rams 6 vehicles
articles.summary: A sport utility vehicle (SUV) driver was arrested after his vehicle rammed into three cars and four motorcycles, killing one person and injuring at least six others as it traveled from Tomas Morato…

blocks.text: A sport utility vehicle (SUV) driver was arrested after his vehicle rammed into three cars and four motorcycles, killing one person and injuring at least six others as it traveled from Tomas Morato Avenue toward Elliptical Road in Quezon City around 3 a.m. Sunday, Sept. 6. The Quezon City Police District (QCPD) Traffic Sector 4 identified the SUV driver as alias “Carl.” The SUV was first involved in a collision along Tomas Morato Avenue before heading toward Quezon Avenue, where it crashed again, and later toward Elliptical Road, where it figured in further accidents. Responding personnel from Traffic Sector 4 immediately took the driver into custody. The motorcycle rider was declared dead, while the injured victims were rushed to East Avenue Medical Center and Quezon City General Hospital for treatment. The QCPD is conducting a follow-up investigation to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the successive collisions and the liability of the driver.
