articles.title: PVL: Nxled fends off Ho Chi Minh City to stay in race to final
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.…

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons’ Jonah Sabete-Escamillan rises for a hit during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.

Jonah Sabete-Escamillan continued to display an all-around game with 18 points, 20 excellent receptions, and 15 digs. Myla Pablo also scored 18, highlighted by five blocks, while MJ Phillips chipped in 17 points.
Gel Cayuna dished out 35 excellent sets, as EJ Laure-Cariño had 16 points and 24 excellent receptions, while Jackie Acuña added 12, as Nxled tied PLDT at 2-2.
Nxled, which battles Farm Fresh on Sunday at 1:30 p.m., holds the tie-break advantage with seven points ahead of PLDT’s six.

Hours after a five-set meltdown to EST Cola on Thursday night when they blew a 20-12 lead in the fourth set, the Chameleons squandered another big lead against the Vietnamese, who erased their 19-10 margin and cut it down to one, 22-21, after Dang Thi Kim Thanh’s kill.

blocks.caption: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference.

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
Phillips and Escamillan refused to suffer the same heartbreak, closing out the game with three points including two quick attacks from the former.

“We love to fight because the last game was a five set and it was only a few hours ago. It was really tough and we wanted immediately to show that we never back down, we are not broken, we will never be broken after a losing match and we are ready to fight,” said Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti.

“Obviously, there are bad things and good things. The good thing is this one: we never give up. The bad thing is that we are developing the side out, but we can do even better because sometimes, I joke about this, our side out is kind of bipolar or we play like a super great team or we get scared and under pressure and nothing works, and so it’s a part of the mental game that we have to really develop.”
Dang led the Vietnamese with 15 points and 15 digs. The 16-year-old Ho Thi Bich Diep had 13 points, while Dao Thi Nhung added 11.
Ho Chi Minh bombed out of finals contention with a 1-3 record.

articles.title: Dalaguete vegetable farmer on motorbike shot, killed
articles.summary: A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu....…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu.

Police identified the victim as alias “JR,” a farmer and resident of Barangay Nalhub. Investigators confirmed that the victim died instantly at the scene after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds to various parts of his body.
The incident occurred around 7:15 p.m. while the victim was transporting his produce along the road.
The Dalaguete Municipal Police Station immediately launched an investigation after receiving a call from the Barangay Chairman of Nalhub reporting the shooting.
Initial police findings revealed that the victim was actively maneuvering his motorcycle—which was carrying vegetable baskets (locally known as bukag)—when he was fired upon.
Probe in progress
At the crime scene, forensic investigators recovered two empty shell casings believed to be from a .45 caliber handgun, as well as two misfired rounds of ammunition.
The perpetrator remains unidentified and fled the scene following the attack.
The Dalaguete Police are continuing their investigation to determine the motive and trace the whereabouts of the suspect.

articles.title: Cebuana Lhuillier turns purposeful communication into impact at the Philippine Quill Awards
articles.summary: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education,…

blocks.text: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education, entrepreneurship, and advocacy platforms, the company uses communication to address real needs, create opportunities, and encourage people to learn, participate, and take action.

This approach earned the company Merit recognition at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards across four areas: Internal Communication for Amazing KaCebuana; Corporate Social Responsibility for Money Guro and Happiest Pinoy; Government Relations and Public Affairs for its range of Business Support solutions; and Social Media for Money Guro.

For Cebuana Lhuillier President and CEO Jean Henri Lhuillier, effective communication should create value for the people it reaches. “At Cebuana Lhuillier, communication is not just about telling people what we do. It is about creating something useful for the people we serve,” said Lhuillier. “When communication helps an employee feel valued, gives a Filipino knowledge to make better decisions, equips an entrepreneur to grow, or gives people a reason to believe in themselves and each other, then it has done its job.”
Purpose Across Every Platform
That principle is reflected in each of the company’s recognized initiatives, with every platform built around a distinct audience need.

Within the organization, Amazing KaCebu integrates employee engagement into the everyday work experience. Through platforms such as Workvivo and the Corporate News Ngayon newsletter, which connects thousands of employees across the country, along with the Brillo Awards, leadership programs, and the REBEL wellbeing app, employees have more ways to stay informed, be recognized, be heard, and feel supported.

For navigating everyday financial decisions, Money Guro makes financial education more accessible and relatable by turning complex concepts into practical conversations. Through social media, student engagements, workshops, and even Roblox, it brings financial education closer to Filipinos.

Happiest Pinoy takes a different approach, using storytelling to reflect the Filipino experience. Its 2025 campaign moved beyond the search for a single “happiest” Filipino and opened the platform to stories of hope, recovery, and resilience, giving people space to share experiences and find connection through a shared sense of community.

For entrepreneurs, Cebuana Lhuillier’s suite of business support solutions recognizes that capital is only one part of what MSMEs need to grow. Its digital-first ecosystem brings together business education, expert guidance, tools, mentoring, entrepreneur stories, and financial services to help business owners make better decisions and build capability at every stage of their journey.
What connects these initiatives is a simple approach: start with what people need, then find the right way to reach them.

“What makes these initiatives stand out is how each one starts with a clear audience need and translates it into a communication approach that people can relate to and act on,” said Emirosco Michael Sena, First Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer of Cebuana Lhuillier. “Whether we are engaging our employees, simplifying financial concepts, supporting entrepreneurs, or telling stories of resilience, we look at the right message, platform, and format for each audience. The Merit Awards validate that approach and the work of our teams in turning strong ideas into programs that deliver results.”
Communication That Moves People

Organized by the International Association of Business Communicators (IABC) Philippines, the Philippine Quill Awards recognize excellence in business communication, including strategic thinking, creative execution, and results.

For Cebuana Lhuillier, the recognition reinforces the role communication can play beyond corporate messaging. Done with purpose, it can help employees feel connected, make knowledge more accessible, strengthen entrepreneurs, and create space for stories that matter.
Ultimately, the goal is not simply to be heard. It is to create communication that leaves people with something they can use, act on, or carry forward.
ADVT.
This article is brought to you by Cebuana Lhuillier.

articles.title: Zheng Qinwen back in the hunt–and US Open third round
articles.summary: NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of…

blocks.text: FILE–Qinwen Zheng of China. (AP Photo/Maja Smiejkowska)

NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of her game — and her competitive fire.
The former world number four endured an injury-plagued 2025 that included a longer than anticipated recovery from elbow surgery.
She missed the Australian Open and has struggled to regain her form, and the mindset of a champion.
“Before the surgery, for me winning is like drinking water — everything comes natural, everything comes fluent,” Zheng said after beating Yulia Putintseva 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 to reach the third round.
“After my surgery, I had some tough matches against the best players in the world (and) I’m close but I don’t get them.
“I totally lost the dynamic of how to compete.
“Now after two, three months I really felt the first time in this tournament I find myself, I found my fire back during the competition.”
Zheng sank so far in the rankings that she had to go through qualifying to book her US Open berth.
She grudgingly acknowledged that grinding through the qualifiers may have helped her regain her competitive edge — but that didn’t really take the sting away.
“It takes a while for me to accept my ranking dropped to 125 and, OK, I need to actually play qualies,” she said.
Now she’s in the thick of the main draw and will face former Australian Open champion Keys for a place in the last 16.
Zheng is looking forward to the test — and likely a chance to step back onto one of the main show courts of Flushing Meadows after toiling through two rounds on the outside courts.
“I used to always play on the big court,” she said. “I need to fight to get everything back.”

articles.title: Over half of targeted kinds injected vs measles, rubella in Ilocos Region
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A total of 272,096 children, or 61.2 percent of the target population, have been vaccinated against measles and rubella in the Ilocos Region as of Sept. 2, according to…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A total of 272,096 children, or 61.2 percent of the target population, have been vaccinated against measles and rubella in the Ilocos Region as of Sept. 2, according to the latest “Ligtas Tigdas” bulletin.
The vaccination campaign covers children aged 6 months to 59 months across the region.
Among the age groups, children aged 24 to 59 months accounted for the largest number of vaccinated at 186,926, representing 63 percent coverage.
This was followed by 50,180 vaccinated children aged 13 to 23 months, or 55.6 percent, and 34,900 children vaccinated aged 6 to 12 months, or 60.7 percent.
Ilocos Norte posted the highest coverage at 90.2 percent, with 38,442 children vaccinated.
Ilocos Sur followed with 40,657 vaccinated, or 83.5 percent coverage, while La Union recorded 42,586 or 68 percent.
Pangasinan had 139,307 vaccinated children, equivalent to 50.6 percent coverage, while Dagupan City recorded 11,104 or 72.2 percent.
Several local governments have already surpassed the 95-percent measles-rubella vaccination coverage target.
Batac City in Ilocos Norte was the first city in the region to reach the target, recording 98 percent coverage.
Among municipalities, Currimao led with 105.5 percent, followed by Dingras at 105.1 percent and Carasi at 104.2 percent.
Bantay in Ilocos Sur recorded 101 percent, while Marcos posted 97.5 percent, Piddig 96.4 percent, Solsona 96.1 percent, Pinili 96 percent and Pagudpud 95.7 percent.
Health authorities encourage parents and guardians to have eligible children vaccinated as the campaign seeks to increase protection against measles and rubella across the region. /apl
—Kenneth P. Tabin / Contributor

articles.title: Yvon Bisera shooting for two birds at LPGT Summit Point stop
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City…

blocks.text: Yvon Bisera has two wins in the LPGT season thus far. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City in Batangas.
Bisera will not just be seeking to win another P1 million event, but also use this stint to sharpen her game for a first appearance in the lucrative yet tougher Korean LPGA later this month.

“I want to play well at Summit Point and use it to prepare for Korea,” said Bisera, who will play in the Hana Financial Group Championship from Sept. 17-20 in Gyeonggi Province, on Daebudo Island southwest of Seoul.

Bisera has been in impressive form on the LPGT this season, outlasting two rivals in a playoff to capture the Lakewood Championship in March. She then produced an emphatic seven-shot victory at the Pradera Verde Championship last July, and those victories have certainly established her as a favorite in Lipa.
With her Korean LPGA debut fast approaching, Bisera has used her time between tournaments to fine-tune the part of her game she believes could prove decisive at Summit Point: the short game.

While waiting for her Korean visa documents, the Davaoeña has devoted extra time to sharpening her touch around the greens, particularly with the possibility of strong winds adding another layer of difficulty at the Batangas layout.
“You can’t lose focus at Summit Point, especially in the face of strong winds,” Bisera continued in Filipino.
That focus will be particularly crucial in a 54-hole event, where a fast start can provide early advantage.
Bisera, however, is not expecting another runaway performance like the one she produced at Pradera Verde.
“I really want to win, but everyone in the field has been preparing hard for this tournament,” she said. “But I will try my best to perform well for my confidence going to Korea.”

She will have plenty of opposition in Batangas, with reigning Order of Merit champion Sarah Ababa leading a compact but formidable field that also features former leg winners Mafy Singson, Tiffany Lee, Chihiro Ikeda and Princess Superal.

Korean challenger Kim Seoyun is likewise expected to figure prominently, along with title-hungry contenders Martina Miñoza, Pamela Mariano, Velinda Castil, Rev Alcantara, Angela Mangana and Gretchen Villacencio.

articles.title: Cebu, Bohol anti-drug ops target 129 cannabis, ₱238K shabu
articles.summary: Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in separate anti-illegal drug operations on Thursday, September 3.
The operations were conducted by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 7 (PDEA 7), Philippine National Police (PNP) units and other law enforcement agencies.
Marijuana in Toledo
Around 11:08 a.m., combined law enforcement elements uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants from a cultivation site in Sitio Guincamote, Barangay Captain Claudio, Toledo City.
Authorities reached the site after an over eight-hour trek.
The operation stemmed from information provided by a confidential informant, followed by about one month of case buildup, according to authorities.

The operation involved personnel from the PDEA Cebu Provincial Office, Naval Forces Central, PNP Drug Enforcement Group–Special Operations Unit 7, Cebu Provincial Police Office–Provincial Intelligence Unit, CPPO–2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company, and Toledo City Police Station.
PDEA 7 identified the suspected cultivator as alias Gene, a resident of Barangay Captain Claudio, who fled the scene before authorities could arrest him.
The 129 marijuana plants had an estimated value of ₱25,800.

Representative samples of the seized plants were turned over to the PDEA 7 Regional Office Laboratory, while the remaining plants were burned on site following protocols established for the disposition of dangerous drugs.
Authorities said a case for cultivation of dangerous drugs under Section 16, Article II of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, will be filed against Gene.
Shabu in Tagbilaran
Later that day, around 5:24 p.m., authorities arrested another drug personality in a buy-bust operation at Purok 4, Barangay Bool, Tagbilaran City, Bohol.
The operation was conducted by the PDEA Bohol Provincial Office, Tagbilaran Police Station and Bohol Maritime Police.

Authorities acted on information from a confidential informant and conducted about one week of case buildup before the buy-bust operation.The suspect was identified as alias Kalaw, 38, unemployed and a resident of Barangay Tangnan, Panglao, Bohol.
Seized during the operation were three packs of shabu weighing around 35 grams, with an estimated average market value of ₱238,000.
Authorities also seized the buy-bust money and a cell phone.
Authorities said Kalaw had allegedly been disposing of around 50 grams of shabu weekly.
The seized dangerous drugs were turned over to the PNP Bohol Forensic Unit for proper disposition.
As of Friday, September 4, Kalaw remains in the custody of the Tagbilaran Police Station.
He is set to face charges for the sale and possession of dangerous drugs under Sections 5 and 11, Article II of Republic Act 9165.
The two operations resulted in the seizure of illegal drugs with a combined estimated value of ₱263,800, including the ₱25,800 worth of marijuana plants and ₱238,000 worth of shabu.

articles.title: Yeng Constantino says husband Victor doesn’t get jealous of Ryan Bang
articles.summary: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.…

blocks.text: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.

Constantino was asked during an ambush interview after the media conference for “The Voice Kids” on Friday, Sept. 4, in Quezon City, whether her husband minds that her and Bang’s courting history recently renewed attention online.

“Sana nga nagseselos eh,” she joked. “Hindi nya kasi personality. Talagang ano sya, very understanding. Kilalang kilala kasi ako ng asawa ko. Alam nya ‘yung pagkanta ko kay Ryan ay nangungulit lamang ako. Actually, mas nakaka-emphatize nga siya kay Ryan kaysa sa akin.”
Constantino said Asuncion and Bang are not close friends, but she hopes that one day, the three of them will get to hang out together.
The story stemmed from Constantino “Biyaheng Bente: 20th Anniversary Concert” on Aug. 28, where she serenaded Bang and recalled their “almost” romance from their early years in show business.
Constantino previously revealed that she had a huge crush on Ryan but felt hurt when he stopped pursuing her.
Bang, for his part, explained that he thought the singer was not interested in him as he admitted that he was also “financially incapable” of dating someone at the time.
After the concert, Bang became emotional during the Sept. 2 episode of “It’s Showtime” while recalling his experience at Constantino’s concert.
He thanked Vice Ganda for bringing him to the show, saying it brought back good memories.
Bang, who has since become single following his split from former fiancée Paola Huyong earlier this year, wondered whether he would ever find someone like Constantino again.
Constantino said she did not expect her playful interaction with Bang at the concert to have such an emotional impact, noting that now she feels slightly regretful about singing to him.

“I was being playful. Hindi ko nga rin po alam ang naging resulta ng aking aksyon. At nag-cost nga na maungkat ang mga sugat. I’m really regretful din in a way. Siyempre nakita mo yung tao na may mga naalala siya. Nakasakit sa kanya. Masakit. Kasi ako, parang nagbibiro ako. Hindi ako nakapag-isip ng maayos to consider his feelings,” she said.
The “Chinito” singer noted that she had already reached out to Bang to apologize.

“Nag-message na po kami sa kanya. Talagang grabe ang sorry ko sa kanya. Ang haba po ng mga nobelang messages namin ni Ryan. Patawarin nyo po ako. Sorry talaga. Hindi ko alam na ganito. And it was really vulnerable. I really apologized for triggering some memories or moments in life namin. I wasn’t very mindful also,” she said.
When asked about Bang’s remark that he hoped he would someday find someone like Constantino, the singer assured him that he would find love.
“Siyempre naman. Naku, makakahanap at makakahanap si Ryan. Hindi deserve ni Ryan na questionin niya ang kanyang worth,” she said.

“Sa pagkakakilala ko po kay Ryan, talagang napakabait po na tao. What a good man. God has perfect timing for everybody. He deserves to be loved, to be cared for, to be seen. He deserves all of that,” she expressed.
Meanwhile, Constantino is one of the new judges of “The Voice Kids,” alongside Gloc-9 and returning judge Julie Anne San Jose. The new season premieres on GMA on Sept. 13. /apl

articles.title: Pedestrian, motorcycle rider dead in separate accidents in Rizal
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — A pedestrian and a motorcycle rider died in separate road accidents in Rizal province on Thursday, Sept. 3, police said. The Calabarzon police, in a report on Friday. (September 4),…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — A pedestrian and a motorcycle rider died in separate road accidents in Rizal province on Thursday, Sept. 3, police said.
The Calabarzon police, in a report on Friday. (September 4), said the a road mishap happened along Marcos Highway in Barangay San Jose at Antipolo City in the early hours of Thursday.
A 22-year-old motorcycle rider was traveling when he reportedly overshot the curb, crossed into the opposite lane, and crashed into a parked vehicle along the roadside.
The impact threw the rider off his motorcycle, and landed on the pavement.
He was rushed to the nearest hospital for his severe head injuries but was declared dead on arrival.
The police report did not indicate whether the rider was wearing a protective helmet, as required under Republic Act No. 10054, or the Motorcycle Helmet Act of 2009.
Meanwhile, police also reported that a 35-year-old female pedestrian died after she was struck by a motorcycle at around 7:30 p.m. while crossing a street in Barangay Plaza Aldea at Tanay town.
The woman sustained fatal injuries and was brought to a local hospital before being transferred to the Rizal Provincial Hospital System in Antipolo City. She was declared dead on arrival.
Police said the kin of those involved were working toward an amicable settlement. /apl

articles.title: Gilas Pilipinas meets familiar face in Rhenz Abando in Korea
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines— Gilas Pilipinas saw a familiar face in Korea during its preparation for the 2026 Asian Games. In a Facebook post by Adrian Nocum, the Nationals were seen dining with Anyang JKJ’s…

blocks.text: KBL standout Rhenz Abando and Gilas Pilipinas players bound for the Asian Games. –ADRIAN NOCUM
MANILA, Philippines— Gilas Pilipinas saw a familiar face in Korea during its preparation for the 2026 Asian Games.
In a Facebook post by Adrian Nocum, the Nationals were seen dining with Anyang JKJ’s Filipino import and former Gilas swingman Rhenz Abando.
“Kain po tayo,” wrote Nocum in a post that also featured Converge twin towers Justin Arana and Justine Baltazar, Barangay Ginebra’s RJ Abarrientos and San Miguel Beer’s Don Trollano.
Nocum’s post gained traction among netizens, with some even speculating that Abando could be a last-minute addition to Gilas to replace the questionable Justin Brownlee.
No such news, however, has been confirmed, as the meal was simply a reunion since Abando is staying in Korea for his stint in the KBL.
Abando last suited up for Gilas in the 2023 Fiba World Cup.
Coincidentally, Nocum and Abando’s meeting was an NCAA reunion of sorts, as they faced each other in the Season 97 Finals between Mapua and Letran.
Since then, Abando joined the KBL, while Nocum declared for the PBA Draft before ultimately being selected by Rain or Shine.

articles.title: MIMAROPA cops, DENR seize P63.7K worth of forest products in one day
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police and environment authorities arrested two people and seized forest products worth an estimated over P63,000 in separate anti-illegal logging operations in…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police and environment authorities arrested two people and seized forest products worth an estimated over P63,000 in separate anti-illegal logging operations in Romblon and Palawan on Thursday (Sept. 3).

The Police Regional Office in MIMAROPA said the operations were conducted with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to curb illegal cutting and possession of forest products in the region.
MIMAROPA covers the southwestern Tagalog region composed of Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon and Palawan.

In San Fernando town in Romblon, personnel of the San Fernando Municipal Police Station provided security assistance to the DENR-Protected Area Management Office in Sibuyan during an anti-illegal logging operation in Sitio Olango, Barangay España.
At about 9:45 a.m., a 40-year-old resident was reportedly caught holding an axe beside a freshly-cut Balaw tree measuring about 30 centimeters in diameter and 30 feet long.
The tree was estimated to have a volume of 273.9 board feet, with a value of P13,695.
The suspect was brought to the San Fernando police station.

Authorities prepared charges against the arrested person for alleged violation of Section 77 of Presidential Decree No. 705, or the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines, as amended by Executive Order No. 277.
Meanwhile, in Palawan town of Roxas, the personnel of the Roxas Municipal Police Station enforced a search warrant against a 69-year-old resident of Purok Zambales in Barangay 3.
They moved together with the DENR, Palawan Provincial Intelligence Unit, and 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company.
The warrant was issued in connection with an alleged violation of Section 77 of PD 705.
Authorities recovered assorted forest products, including Ipil lumber and planted Mahogany trees, with an estimated combined volume of 300 board feet and market value of P50,000.
Police said the suspect failed to present valid documents, permits or licenses authorizing the possession and ownership of the forest products.
The seized items were inventoried in the presence of barangay and media workers.
The suspect was brought to the Roxas police station. /apl

articles.title: Globe helps parents guide children's digital journey with GPlan Junior
articles.summary: As children spend more time online for learning, communication, entertainment, and everyday activities, many parents are looking for ways to support their growing digital needs while maintaining…

blocks.text: As children spend more time online for learning, communication, entertainment, and everyday activities, many parents are looking for ways to support their growing digital needs while maintaining appropriate guidance and oversight.
GPlan Junior was created to give kids the freedom to stay connected while giving parents greater peace of mind.
— Jo Anne Illescas-Pique
Senior Director for Globe Postpaid

To help families navigate this stage, Globe has introduced GPlan Junior, a dedicated postpaid line designed for dependents aged 7 to 20 years old. Available as an additional line under an existing Globe Postpaid Plan 999 and above, the offering provides reliable connectivity for children and students while allowing parents and legal guardians to manage the account under their supervision.

The initiative reflects Globe’s commitment to strengthening family connectivity by helping parents support their children’s digital experiences during the years when independence is growing but adult guidance remains important.

blocks.caption: GPlan Junior helps families keep children connected while giving parents greater visibility and control over their digital experiences. | Photo by Globe

blocks.text: For Php499 per month, GPlan Junior comes with unlimited calls and texts, 100-minutes of landline calls, 10GB of all-access data, free access to Messenger Kids and Mobile Legends, and unlimited access to three selected apps across video, social, and gaming categories.
Families may choose one app from each category:

items: Video: YouTube Kids, Netflix, Disney+, or Viu
Social: Viber or WhatsApp
Play: PUBG, Call of Duty, Discord, or Roblox

blocks.text: By linking a dependent’s mobile line to a parent’s Globe Postpaid account, GPlan Junior addresses the need for frequent reloads and monitoring expiring prepaid promos. This allows families to enjoy a more seamless connectivity experience while helping ensure that children remain connected when they need to be.

The plan’s 10GB-swappable data and with roll-over feature open access data and unlimited access to selected apps support the online activities that many children and students engage in daily, from messaging and video streaming to gaming and communication. At the same time, families benefit from more predictable monthly connectivity spending and reduced concerns about unexpected usage.

Parents can also monitor their child’s data usage through the GlobeOne app, allowing them to track consumption, view remaining allocations, and select Unli Apps, and the preferred Data Swap option. This gives families greater visibility and control while helping children develop more mindful and responsible digital activities and behaviors.

“As children become more connected, parents are looking for solutions that keep up with their family’s evolving needs,” said Jo Anne Illescas-Pique, Senior Director for Globe Postpaid. “GPlan Junior was created to give kids the freedom to stay connected while giving parents greater peace of mind through a simple, reliable Postpaid experience. It’s another way Globe is making technology work better for families and helping them stay connected to what matters most.”
Beyond connectivity, Globe is also encouraging families to build responsible digital and financial habits through an exclusive GCash Jr. incentive.

Eligible GPlan Junior subscribers who successfully sign up for GCash Jr. may receive up to Php500 worth of GCash vouchers. The initiative supports parents who want to introduce children to responsible money management and digital financial literacy at an early age while guiding how they learn, spend, save, and engage with digital financial tools in a supervised environment.

Together, GPlan Junior and GCash Jr. support Globe’s broader goal of helping families navigate an increasingly connected world with greater confidence while fostering responsible digital citizenship among the next generation.

Parents or legal guardians interested in applying may visit any Globe Store and present any proof of eligibility, including a copy of the dependent’s PSA Birth Certificate and a valid ID, such as a school ID or passport, to verify guardianship and age.
For more information, visit the nearest Globe Store or go to globe.com.ph.

articles.title: 2 deaths recorded in Olongapo due to leptospirosis
articles.summary: OLONGAPO CITY — As flooding persisted in several areas in this city, two people died of leptospirosis, based on data from the Olongapo City Health Office. As of Sept. 3, the city had recorded 27…

blocks.text: OLONGAPO CITY — As flooding persisted in several areas in this city, two people died of leptospirosis, based on data from the Olongapo City Health Office.
As of Sept. 3, the city had recorded 27 leptospirosis cases, of which 18 remained active.
Fourteen of the active cases were admitted at hospitals, four were being treated as outpatients, while seven patients have recovered from the disease.
The local government and the city health office reminded residents to avoid wading or playing in floodwaters, especially if they have open wounds.

The health office said free doxycycline was available at its office and at all barangay health centers for residents who had been submerged in floodwaters or those might need to wade through floods again.
Residents were advised to consult health personnel before taking doxycycline for proper use and dosage. /apl

articles.title: Teachers for barangay elections: DepEd Mandaue on prep mode
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) in Mandaue City is preparing teachers who may be tapped to serve in the November Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).... Keep on reading: Teachers…

blocks.text: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — The Department of Education (DepEd) in Mandaue City is preparing teachers who may be tapped to serve in the November Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

Edgar Espina, administrative officer of the DepEd Mandaue City Schools Division, said the department has been coordinating with the Commission on Elections and is prepared to provide the teachers needed for the elections.

“DepEd is really prepared with the election. Andam na ta daan sa gipangayo sa Comelec, naghuwat ra pod ta if madayon o dili basta we have to continue our job, we will not stop kung unsa ang mandate sa DepEd, we will continue. Nag-agad ra pod tas taas if madayon o dili basta kami we are working for it mahuman amoang trabaho with regards to BSKE, Espina said.
(We are ready for whatever Comelec may ask of us; we are only waiting to know if the elections push through. We await the word of the higherups but we have to finish our job.)
Marshaling of frontliners
Espina said the teachers are currently being asked to signify their interest in serving in the elections, while the specific schedules for seminars and orientations will depend on the Comelec.
He said the number that will be sought by Comelec would likely be more than 1,000 teachers basing on previous elections.
Espina said that there were already initial schedules for teachers orientations but the division is awaiting if the elections push through.
Espina said teachers who have relatives involved in local politics may be assigned to another barangay to avoid possible conflicts of interest.
Responsive volunteers
He added that while election service is voluntary, teachers have historically responded to the need for personnel during elections and many continue to serve when called upon.
The preparations come as the November 2026 BSKE remains on the electoral calendar, although there have been proposals seeking to postpone the polls.

Senate Bill No. 2387, sponsored by Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, seeks to set the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials at five years, which would move the scheduled November 2026 elections to November 2028.

The last BSKE was held in October 2023 and was originally expected to be held again in 2025. The elections were postponed to November 2026 after the terms of incumbent barangay and SK officials were extended to four years.

articles.title: Alex Eala’s growing star power draws US media attention
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–Filipino tennis star Alex Eala continues to be the talk of the town as her meteoric rise draws attention from some of the United States’ biggest publications. Eala landed on the…

blocks.text: Alex Eala Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, reacts during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships against Oleksandra Oliynykova, of Ukraine, Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in New York
MANILA, Philippines–Filipino tennis star Alex Eala continues to be the talk of the town as her meteoric rise draws attention from some of the United States’ biggest publications.

Eala landed on the front page of The New York Times for its September 3 print issue, highlighting her impact on the Filipino community at home and overseas, particularly in Queens, where the US Open is being held.

“But for Filipinos, she is not simply an ambassador for the sport. Her success is giving the country, a large, dispersed archipelago of more than 7,000 islands in Southeast Asia, as well as its diaspora, a reason to unite,” the article said.
Eala also landed an in-depth feature in Vogue, which highlighted the growing frenzy around the 21-year-old star and the Filipino fans who have followed her matches.

blocks.caption: Fans of Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, spell out "GO ALEX" with letters before her match against Mary Stoiana, of the United States, in the first round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, in New York.

blocks.text: Fans of Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, spell out “GO ALEX” with letters before her match against Mary Stoiana, of the United States, in the first round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)
Forbes, meanwhile, noted Eala’s growing commercial value and projected that she could become one of the world’s highest-paid female athletes.

“I feel very confident that by 2027, she will be the second-highest-paid female athlete in the world, behind Coco [Gauff],” Max Eisenbud, head of client representation at WME Sports and its subsidiary IMG Tennis, was quoted as saying.
She also graced the digital cover of Sports Illustrated, which dubbed her “tennis’s next great superstar,” while The New Yorker published a story on how Eala “became a symbol of the Philippines.”
The stories have highlighted Eala’s rise to prominence and how it has helped Filipinos once again find someone to rally behind, much like during the heyday of Filipino boxing legend Manny Pacquiao.
Eala has been vocal about knowing what it means to carry the country wherever she goes, and fans have reciprocated that love by filling the stands during her tournaments.

“I think everybody represents something in their own way. I’m Filipino and I proudly represent that and a lot of the crowd here today is Filipino and I’m sure they share in that sentiment,” Eala said after her second-round victory at the US Open.
Eala continues her campaign in the last Grand Slam tournament of the season in the third round.
